verses.text:
1:2but his will is in the Lord’s law,
and on His law he will meditate day and night.

1:3He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters,
which will give its fruit in its season,
and whose leaf will not fall off;
and everything he does will be prospered.

1:4Not so the ungodly, not so,
but like chaff which the wind flings away from the face of the earth.

1:5Therefore the ungodly will not rise in judgment,
nor sinners in the council of the righteous;

1:6for the Lord knows the way of the righteous,
and the way of the ungodly will perish.

2:1Why did nations rage,
and peoples meditate on empty things?

2:2The kings of the earth stood ready,
and the rulers gathered together,
against the Lord and against His anointed.
Diapsalma.

2:3“Let us tear apart their bonds
and cast their yoke away from us.”

2:4The One dwelling in heaven will laugh at them,
and the Lord will sneer at them.

2:5Then He will speak to them in His anger
and trouble them in His fury:

2:6“But I was appointed king by Him
on Zion, His holy mountain,

2:8Ask of Me, and I will give you nations as your inheritance,
and the ends of the earth as your possession.

2:9You will shepherd them with an iron rod;
you will crush them like a potter’s vessel.’”

2:10And now, kings, understand;
be instructed, all who judge the earth.

2:11Serve the Lord with fear,
and exult in Him with trembling.

2:12Take hold of instruction, lest the Lord become angry
and you perish from a righteous way.
When His fury burns quickly,
blessed are all who have trusted in Him.
3:1A psalm of David, when he was fleeing from the presence of Absalom his son.

3:2Lord, why have those who afflict me multiplied?
Many rise up against me.

3:3Many say to my soul,
“There is no salvation for him in his God.”
Diapsalma.

3:4But Thou, Lord, art my helper,
my glory and the One who lifts my head.

3:5With my voice I cried to the Lord,
and He heard me from His holy mountain.
Diapsalma.

3:6I lay down and slept;
I was awakened, for the Lord will help me.

3:7I will not fear tens of thousands of people
who together attack me all around.

3:9Salvation belongs to the Lord,
and Thy blessing is upon Thy people.
4:1For the end, among psalms. A song of David.

4:2When I called, the God of my righteousness heard me.
In affliction Thou madest room for me.
Have compassion on me, and hear my prayer.

4:3Sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart?
Why do you love vanity and seek falsehood?
Diapsalma.

4:4Know that the Lord has made His holy one wondrous;
the Lord will hear me when I cry to Him.

4:5Be angry, and do not sin;
speak in your hearts,
and upon your beds be pierced with remorse.
Diapsalma.

4:6Offer a sacrifice of righteousness,
and hope in the Lord.

4:7Many say, “Who will show us good things?”
The light of Thy face was marked upon us, Lord.

4:8Thou didst put gladness in my heart;
from the season of their grain and wine and oil, they were increased.

4:9In peace I will both lie down and sleep,
for Thou, Lord, madest me dwell alone in hope.
5:1For the end, concerning her who inherits. A psalm of David.

5:2Give ear to my words, Lord;
understand my cry.

5:3Attend to the voice of my petition,
my King and my God,
for unto Thee I will pray, Lord.

5:4In the morning Thou wilt hear my voice;
in the morning I will stand before Thee and watch.

5:5For Thou art not a God who desires lawlessness,
nor will an evildoer sojourn with Thee.

5:6The lawless will not remain before Thine eyes;
Thou didst hate all who work lawlessness.

5:7Thou wilt destroy all who speak falsehood;
the Lord abhors a man of bloodshed and deceit.

5:8But I, through the multitude of Thy mercy, will enter Thy house;
I will bow toward Thy holy temple in fear of Thee.

5:9Lord, guide me in Thy righteousness because of my enemies;
direct Thy way straight before me.

5:11Judge them, God!
Let them fall away from their counsels.
According to the multitude of their ungodly deeds, drive them out,
for they provoked Thee bitterly, Lord.

5:13For Thou wilt bless the righteous one;
Lord, Thou didst crown us as with a weapon of favor.
6:1For the end, among hymns, concerning the eighth. A psalm of David.

6:2Lord, do not rebuke me in Thy fury,
nor discipline me in Thine anger.

6:3Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak;
heal me, Lord, for my bones were troubled,

6:4and my soul was greatly troubled.
And Thou, Lord—how long?

6:5Return, Lord; rescue my soul.
Save me for the sake of Thy mercy.

6:6For in death there is no one who remembers Thee;
and in Hades, who will give Thee thanks?

6:8My eye was troubled from anger;
I grew old among all my enemies.

6:9Stand away from me, all who work lawlessness,
for the Lord heard the voice of my weeping.

6:10The Lord heard my petition;
the Lord accepted my prayer.

6:11May all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled;
may they turn back and be greatly put to shame quickly.
7:1A psalm of David, which he sang to the Lord concerning the words of Chousi son of Iemeni.

7:2Lord my God, in Thee I hoped.
Save me from all who pursue me, and rescue me,

7:3lest he seize my soul like a lion,
with no one to redeem or save.

7:4Lord my God, if I did this,
if there is injustice in my hands,

7:5if I repaid those who repay me evils,
then may I fall away from my enemies empty,

7:6then may the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it,
trample my life into the earth,
and make my glory dwell in dust.
Diapsalma.

7:8and an assembly of peoples will surround Thee;
and for its sake return on high.

7:9The Lord will judge peoples.
Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness
and according to my innocence upon me.

7:10Let sinners’ wickedness come to an end,
and Thou wilt direct the righteous one,
God who tests hearts and kidneys.

7:11Righteous is my help from God,
who saves those upright in heart.

7:12God is a righteous judge, strong and patient,
not bringing wrath every day.

7:13If you do not return, He will polish His sword;
He bent His bow and prepared it,

7:14and in it He prepared instruments of death;
He fashioned His arrows for those being burned.

7:15Behold, he was in labor with injustice;
he conceived trouble and gave birth to lawlessness.

7:16He dug a pit and hollowed it out,
and he will fall into the hole he made.

7:17His trouble will return upon his head,
and his injustice will descend upon his crown.

7:18I will give thanks to the Lord according to His righteousness,
and sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.
8:1For the end, concerning the winepresses. A psalm of David.

8:2Lord our Lord, how wondrous is Thy name in all the earth,
for Thy magnificence was raised above the heavens.

8:3From the mouth of infants and nursing children Thou didst prepare praise,
because of Thine enemies,
to bring down the enemy and the avenger.

8:4For I will see the heavens, works of Thy fingers,
the moon and stars which Thou didst found:

8:5what is a human being, that Thou rememberest him,
or a son of man, that Thou visitest him?

8:6Thou madest him a little lower than angels;
Thou didst crown him with glory and honor,

8:7and didst appoint him over the works of Thy hands;
Thou didst subject everything beneath his feet:

8:8all sheep and cattle,
and also the animals of the plain,

8:9the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea,
those that travel along the paths of seas.

8:10Lord our Lord,
how wondrous is Thy name in all the earth!
9:1For the end, concerning the hidden things of the son. A psalm of David.

9:2I will give thanks unto Thee, Lord, with my whole heart;
I will recount all Thy wonders.

9:3I will rejoice and exult in Thee;
I will sing praise to Thy name, Most High.

9:4When my enemy turns back,
they will grow weak and perish before Thee,

9:5for Thou hast upheld my judgment and my cause;
Thou sattest on a throne, Thou who judgest righteousness.

9:6Thou didst rebuke nations, and the ungodly one perished;
Thou didst erase their name for ever and for the age of the age.

9:7The enemy’s swords failed utterly, and Thou didst pull down cities;
their memory perished with a noise.

9:8And the Lord remains for ever;
He prepared His throne for judgment,

9:9and He will judge the inhabited world in righteousness;
He will judge peoples with uprightness.

9:10And the Lord became a refuge for the needy,
a helper at fitting times in distress.

9:11Let those who know Thy name hope in Thee,
for Thou hast not abandoned those who seek Thee, Lord.

9:12Sing praise to the Lord, who dwells in Zion;
announce His deeds among the nations,

9:13for He who calls bloodshed to account remembered them;
He did not forget the cry of the needy.

9:16Nations became fixed in the destruction they brought about;
in this trap they concealed, their foot was caught.

9:18Let sinners turn back to Hades,
all nations that forget God.

9:19For the poor will not be forgotten utterly;
the endurance of the needy will not perish for ever.

9:20Arise, Lord; do not let a human being grow strong;
let nations be judged before Thee.

9:22Why, Lord, hast Thou stood far away,
overlooking us at fitting times in distress?

9:23As the ungodly man exalts himself, the poor man is set ablaze;
they are caught in the counsels they devise.

9:24For the sinner is praised for the desires of his soul,
and the one who acts unjustly is blessed.

9:27For he said in his heart, “I will certainly not be shaken,
from generation to generation, without adversity.”

9:28His mouth is full of cursing, bitterness, and deceit;
under his tongue are toil and trouble.

9:31In his trap he will humble him;
he will bow down and fall as he lords it over the needy.

9:32For he said in his heart, “God has forgotten;
He turned His face away so as never to see.”

9:33Arise, Lord God; let Thy hand be raised;
do not forget the needy.

9:34For what reason did the ungodly provoke God?
For he said in his heart, “He will not call to account.”

9:35Thou seest, for Thou perceivest trouble and anger,
to hand them over into Thy hands.
To Thee, therefore, the poor man has been left;
Thou wast helping the orphan.

9:36Crush the arm of the sinful and evil man;
his sin will be sought out, and he will certainly not be found because of it.

9:37The Lord will reign for ever and for the age of the age;
you will perish, nations, from His land.

9:38The Lord heard the desire of the needy;
Thine ear attended to the preparation of their heart,

9:39to judge for the orphan and the lowly,
so that a human being on the earth may no longer boast greatly.

10:1For the end. A psalm of David.
In the Lord I have trusted.
How will you say to my soul,
“Move away to the mountains like a little bird”?

10:3For what Thou didst establish, they pulled down;
but what did the righteous person do?

10:5The Lord examines the righteous and the ungodly;
but the one who loves injustice hates his own soul.

10:6He will rain traps upon sinners;
fire, sulfur, and a storm wind are the portion of their cup.

10:7For the Lord is righteous and loved righteous deeds;
His face beheld uprightness.
11:1For the end, concerning the eighth. A psalm of David.

11:2Save me, Lord, for the holy one is gone;
for truths have become few among the sons of men.

11:3Each spoke empty things to his neighbor;
deceitful lips spoke with a heart and a heart.

11:4May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips
and a boastful tongue—

11:5those who said, “We will magnify our tongue;
our lips are our own; who is our lord?”

11:6“Because of the misery of the poor
and because of the groaning of the needy,
now I will arise,” says the Lord.
“I will set him in salvation; I will speak openly in him.”

11:7The sayings of the Lord are pure sayings,
silver tried by fire, tested in the earth,
purified sevenfold.

11:8Thou, Lord, wilt keep us
and preserve us from this generation and for ever.

11:9The ungodly walk around;
according to Thy height, Thou heldest the sons of men in high regard.
12:1For the end. A psalm of David.

12:2How long, Lord, wilt Thou forget me utterly?
How long wilt Thou turn Thy face away from me?

12:3How long shall I place counsels within my soul,
pains within my heart by day?
How long will my enemy be raised above me?

12:4Look; hear me, Lord my God.
Give light to my eyes, lest I fall asleep into death,

12:5lest my enemy say, “I prevailed against him.”
Those who afflict me will exult if I am shaken.

12:6But I have hoped in Thy mercy;
my heart will exult in Thy salvation.
I will sing to the Lord, who has benefited me,
and I will sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.

13:1For the end. A psalm of David.
A fool said in his heart, “There is no God.”
They acted corruptly and became abominable in their practices;
there is no one who shows kindness; there is not even one.

13:2The Lord looked down from heaven upon the sons of men,
to see whether there is anyone who understands or seeks God.

13:4Will all those who practice lawlessness not know?
Those who devour my people as a meal of bread did not call upon the Lord.

13:5There they cowered in fear where there was no fear,
for God is with a righteous generation.

13:6You put a poor man’s counsel to shame,
because the Lord is his hope.

13:7Who will give Israel’s salvation from Zion?
When the Lord turns back His people’s captivity,
let Jacob exult and let Israel rejoice.

14:1A psalm of David.
Lord, who will sojourn in Thy dwelling,
and who will encamp on Thy holy mountain?

14:2One who walks blamelessly and works righteousness,
speaking truth in his heart,

14:3who did not act deceitfully with his tongue,
nor do evil to his neighbor,
and did not take up reproach against those nearest him.

14:5He did not lend his silver at interest
and did not take gifts against innocent people.
The one who does these things will never be shaken.

15:1An inscription of David.
Guard me, Lord, for I have hoped in Thee.

15:2I said to the Lord, “Thou art my Lord,
for Thou hast no need of my good things.”

15:3For the holy ones who are in His land,
He made all His purposes wonderful among them.

15:4Their weaknesses multiplied;
after these things they hurried.
I will certainly not gather their gatherings of bloodshed,
nor will I remember their names through my lips.

15:5The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup;
Thou art the One who restores my inheritance to me.

15:6Measuring cords fell for me among the best places;
indeed, my inheritance is the best for me.

15:7I will bless the Lord, who gave me understanding;
indeed, even until night my kidneys disciplined me.

15:8I kept seeing the Lord before me continually,
because He is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.

15:9Therefore my heart rejoiced, and my tongue exulted;
indeed, even my flesh will dwell in hope,

15:10for Thou wilt not abandon my soul to Hades,
nor let Thy holy one see corruption.

16:2May my judgment come forth from Thy presence;
let my eyes see upright things.

16:3Thou didst test my heart; Thou didst visit by night;
Thou didst try me by fire, and no injustice was found in me,

16:4so that my mouth might not speak human deeds.
Because of the words of Thy lips, I kept hard paths.

16:5Set my steps firmly in Thy paths,
so that my steps may not be shaken.

16:6I cried out, for Thou heardest me, God;
incline Thine ear to me and hear my words.

16:7Make Thy mercies wonderful,
Thou who savest those hoping in Thee
from those who oppose Thy right hand.

16:8Guard me as the pupil of an eye;
in the shelter of Thy wings Thou wilt shelter me,

16:9from the ungodly who made me miserable.
My enemies surrounded my soul.

16:10They shut up their fat;
their mouth spoke arrogance.

16:11Casting me out, they now surrounded me;
they set their eyes to turn aside toward the earth.

16:12They took me up like a lion ready for the hunt
and like a young lion dwelling in hiding places.

16:14Lord, separate them from the few, from the earth,
during their life.
Their belly was filled with Thy hidden things;
they were satisfied with sons
and left the remains to their infants.

16:15But I, in righteousness, will appear before Thy face;
I will be satisfied when Thy glory appears.
17:1For the end. Of the Lord’s servant David, who spoke the words of this song to the Lord on the day the Lord rescued him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

17:2And he said:
I will love Thee, Lord, my strength.

17:4Praising, I will call upon the Lord,
and I will be saved from my enemies.

17:5The birth pangs of death encompassed me,
and torrents of lawlessness threw me into turmoil.

17:6The birth pangs of Hades surrounded me;
the traps of death overtook me.

17:7And when I was afflicted, I called upon the Lord
and cried out to my God.
He heard my voice from His holy temple,
and my cry before Him will enter His ears.

17:10And He bent heaven and came down,
and gloom was beneath His feet.

17:11And He mounted cherubim and flew;
He flew on the wings of winds.

17:13From the far-shining radiance before Him, the clouds passed—
hail and coals of fire.

17:14And the Lord thundered from heaven,
and the Most High gave His voice.

17:15And He sent out arrows and scattered them;
He multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into turmoil.

17:16And the springs of the waters appeared,
and the foundations of the inhabited world were uncovered
at Thy rebuke, Lord,
at the blast of the spirit of Thine anger.

17:17He sent from on high and took me;
He took me to Himself out of many waters.

17:18He will rescue me from my powerful enemies
and from those who hate me, for they grew stronger than I.

17:19They overtook me in the day of my affliction,
and the Lord became my support,

17:20and He brought me out into a spacious place.
He will rescue me because He desired me.
He will rescue me from my powerful enemies
and from those who hate me.

17:21And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness,
and according to the purity of my hands He will repay me,

17:22because I kept the Lord’s ways
and did not act impiously by turning from my God,

17:23because all His judgments are before me,
and I did not put His ordinances away from me.

17:24And I will be blameless with Him
and guard myself from my lawlessness.

17:25And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness
and according to the purity of my hands before His eyes.

17:26With a holy one Thou wilt show Thyself holy,
and with an innocent man Thou wilt be innocent,

17:27and with a chosen one Thou wilt be chosen,
and with a twisted one Thou wilt twist.

17:28For Thou wilt save a lowly people
and humble the eyes of the arrogant.

17:29For Thou wilt light my lamp, Lord;
my God, Thou wilt light my darkness.

17:30For by Thee I will be rescued from a raiding band,
and by my God I will cross over a wall.

17:32For who is God except the Lord?
And who is God except our God?

17:33God girds me with power
and made my way blameless,

17:34He sets my feet firmly like a deer’s
and makes me stand upon the heights,

17:35training my hands for war;
and Thou madest my arms a bronze bow.

17:36And Thou gavest me the protection of my salvation;
Thy right hand supported me,
and Thy discipline set me upright completely,
and Thy discipline itself will teach me.

17:37Thou didst widen my steps beneath me,
and my footprints did not grow weak.

17:38I will pursue my enemies and overtake them,
and I will not turn back until they fail.

17:39I will press them down, and they will certainly be unable to stand;
they will fall beneath my feet.

17:40And Thou didst gird me with power for war;
Thou didst fetter all those who rose against me beneath me,

17:41and Thou madest my enemies turn their backs to me,
and Thou didst destroy those who hated me.

17:42They cried out, and there was no one to save;
they cried to the Lord, and He did not hear them.

17:43And I will grind them fine like dust before the wind;
I will smooth them away like mud in the streets.

17:45At the hearing of the ear, it obeyed me;
foreigners lied to me.

17:46Foreigners grew old
and limped away from their paths.

17:47The Lord lives! Blessed be my God!
Let the God of my salvation be exalted,

17:48the God who gives me acts of vengeance
and subjected peoples beneath me,

17:50Therefore I will thank Thee among the nations, Lord,
and sing praise to Thy name,

17:51magnifying the salvations of His king
and showing mercy to His anointed,
to David and to his seed for ever.
18:1For the end. A psalm of David.

18:2The heavens recount God’s glory,
and the firmament announces the work of His hands.

18:3Day pours forth an utterance to day,
and night announces knowledge to night.

18:4There are no utterances or words
whose voices are not heard.

18:5Their sound went out into all the earth,
and their utterances to the limits of the inhabited world.
In the sun He set His dwelling.

18:6And he is like a bridegroom coming out of his bridal chamber;
he will exult like a giant to run his way.

18:8The Lord’s law is blameless, turning souls;
the Lord’s testimony is trustworthy, making infants wise.

18:9The Lord’s ordinances are upright, rejoicing the heart;
the Lord’s commandment shines afar, giving light to the eyes.

18:10The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring for the age of the age;
the Lord’s judgments are true, justified together,

18:11desirable beyond gold and much precious stone,
and sweeter than honey and honeycomb.

18:12For indeed, Thy servant keeps them;
in keeping them there is great recompense.

18:13Who will understand transgressions?
Cleanse me of my hidden things.

18:15And the sayings of my mouth will be pleasing,
and the meditation of my heart will be before Thee continually,
Lord, my helper and my redeemer.
19:1For the end. A psalm of David.

19:2May the Lord hear you in the day of affliction;
may the name of Jacob’s God protect you.

19:3May He send you help from the sanctuary
and support you from Zion.

19:4May He remember every sacrifice of yours
and make your whole burnt offering fat.
Diapsalma.

19:5May He give you according to your heart
and fulfill all your counsel.

19:6We will exult in your salvation,
and in our God’s name we will be magnified.
May the Lord fulfill all your petitions.

19:8These rely on chariots, and those on horses,
but we will be magnified in the name of the Lord our God.

19:9They were fettered and fell,
but we rose and were set upright.

19:10Lord, save Thy king,
and hear us on whatever day we call upon Thee.
20:1For the end. A psalm of David.

20:2Lord, the king will rejoice in Thy power
and exult greatly in Thy salvation.

20:3Thou gavest him the desire of his soul
and didst not deprive him of the wish of his lips.
Diapsalma.

20:4For Thou didst meet him with blessings of kindness;
Thou didst place upon his head a crown of precious stone.

20:5He asked Thee for life, and Thou gavest it to him,
length of days for the age of the age.

20:6His glory is great in Thy salvation;
Thou wilt bestow glory and magnificence upon him.

20:7For Thou wilt give him blessing for the age of the age;
Thou wilt gladden him with joy in Thy presence.

20:8For the king hopes in the Lord,
and through the Most High’s mercy he will certainly not be shaken.

20:9May your hand be found by all your enemies;
may your right hand find all who hate you.

20:11You will destroy their fruit from the earth
and their seed from the sons of men,

20:12because they directed evils against you;
they devised a counsel they will certainly be unable to establish.

20:13For you will make them turn their backs;
among your remaining ones you will prepare their face.

20:14Be exalted, Lord, in Thy power;
we will sing and make music of Thy mighty acts.
21:1For the end, concerning the help of the morning. A psalm of David.

21:2God, my God, attend to me; why didst Thou abandon me?
Far from my salvation are the words of my transgressions.

21:3My God, I will cry by day, and Thou wilt not hear,
and by night, and not to folly for me.

21:4But Thou dwellest among holy ones,
the praise of Israel.

21:5In Thee our fathers hoped;
they hoped, and Thou didst rescue them.

21:6To Thee they cried out and were saved;
in Thee they hoped and were not put to shame.

21:7But I am a worm and not a human being,
a human reproach and an object of the people’s contempt.

21:8All who watch me sneered at me;
they spoke with their lips and shook their heads:

21:9“He hoped in the Lord; let Him rescue him;
let Him save him, since He desires him.”

21:10For Thou art the One who drew me from the belly,
my hope from my mother’s breasts.

21:11Upon Thee I was cast from the womb;
from my mother’s belly Thou art my God.

21:12Do not stand away from me, for affliction is near,
for there is no one to help.

21:13Many calves surrounded me;
fat bulls encompassed me.

21:14They opened their mouth against me
like a lion seizing prey and roaring.

21:15I was poured out like water,
and all my bones were scattered.
My heart became like wax
melting in the midst of my belly.

21:18I counted all my bones;
but they observed and looked upon me.

21:19They divided my garments among themselves,
and cast a lot for my clothing.

21:20But Thou, Lord, do not put my help far away;
attend to my support.

21:21Rescue my soul from the sword
and my only one from the dog’s hand.

21:22Save me from a lion’s mouth
and my lowliness from the horns of one-horned animals.

21:23I will recount Thy name to my brothers;
in the midst of the assembly I will sing hymns unto Thee:

21:24You who fear the Lord, praise Him!
All Jacob’s seed, glorify Him!
Let all Israel’s seed fear Him,

21:25because He did not despise or resent the poor man’s petition,
nor turn His face away from me,
and when I cried out to Him, He heard me.

21:26From Thee comes my praise in a great assembly;
I will repay my vows before those who fear Him.

21:28All the limits of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord,
and all the families of the nations will bow down before Thee,

21:29because kingship belongs to the Lord,
and He is master of the nations.

21:31And my seed will serve Him;
the coming generation will be announced to the Lord,

21:32and they will announce His righteousness
to a people yet to be born,
because the Lord has done it.

22:1A psalm of David.
The Lord shepherds me, and nothing shall fail me.

22:2He made me dwell in a place of green growth;
He nourished me beside water of rest.

22:6And Thy mercy will pursue me all the days of my life,
and I will dwell in the Lord’s house for length of days.

23:1A psalm of David, for the first day of the week.
The earth and its fullness belong to the Lord,
the inhabited world and all who dwell in it.

23:2He founded it upon seas
and prepared it upon rivers.

23:3Who will ascend the Lord’s mountain,
and who will stand in His holy place?

23:4One innocent in hands and pure in heart,
who did not take up his soul for emptiness
and did not swear deceitfully to his neighbor.

23:5This one will receive blessing from the Lord
and mercy from God his Savior.

23:6This is the generation of those who seek Him,
who seek the face of Jacob’s God.
Diapsalma.

23:7Your rulers—lift up gates!
And be raised, eternal gates,
and the King of glory will enter.

23:9Your rulers—lift up gates!
And be raised, eternal gates,
and the King of glory will enter.

23:10Who is this King of glory?
The Lord of powers—He is the King of glory.

24:1A psalm of David.
To Thee, Lord, I lifted my soul, my God.

24:2In Thee I have trusted; may I not be put to shame,
and let my enemies not laugh at me.

24:3For indeed, all who wait for Thee will certainly not be put to shame;
let all who act lawlessly without cause be ashamed.

24:4Make Thy ways known to me, Lord,
and teach me Thy paths.

24:5Guide me into Thy truth
and teach me, for Thou art God my Savior,
and I waited for Thee the whole day.

24:6Remember Thy compassions, Lord,
and Thy mercies, for they are from eternity.

24:8The Lord is kind and upright;
therefore He will give sinners instruction in the way.

24:9He will guide the meek in judgment;
He will teach the meek His ways.

24:10All the Lord’s ways are mercy and truth
for those who seek His covenant and His testimonies.

24:11For Thy name’s sake, Lord,
Thou wilt be gracious to my sin, for it is great.

24:12Who is the human being who fears the Lord?
He will give him instruction in a way he chose.

24:13His soul will lodge among good things,
and his seed will inherit land.

24:14The Lord is the stronghold of those who fear Him,
and the Lord’s name belongs to those who fear Him,
and His covenant is to make things known to them.

24:15My eyes are continually toward the Lord,
for He will pull my feet out of a trap.

24:16Look upon me and have mercy on me,
for I am alone and poor.

24:17The afflictions of my heart widened;
bring me out of my distresses.

24:18See my humiliation and my toil,
and forgive all my sins.

24:19See my enemies, for they multiplied
and hated me with unjust hatred.

24:20Guard my soul and rescue me;
may I not be put to shame, for I hoped in Thee.

24:21Innocent and upright people clung to me,
for I waited for Thee, Lord.

24:22Redeem Israel, God,
from all its afflictions.

25:1Of David.
Judge me, Lord, for I walked in my innocence,
and hoping in the Lord, I will certainly not grow weak.

25:2Test me, Lord, and try me;
try my kidneys and my heart by fire.

25:3For Thy mercy is before my eyes,
and I acted pleasingly in Thy truth.

25:4I did not sit with a council of emptiness,
and I will certainly not enter with transgressors.

25:5I hated an assembly of evildoers,
and I will certainly not sit with the ungodly.

25:6I will wash my hands among the innocent
and go around Thine altar, Lord,

25:7to hear a voice of praise
and recount all Thy wonders.

25:8Lord, I loved the beauty of Thy house
and the place of Thy glory’s dwelling.

25:9Do not destroy my soul together with the ungodly,
or my life with men of bloodshed,

25:10in whose hands are lawless deeds;
their right hand was filled with gifts.

25:11But I walked in my innocence;
redeem me and have mercy on me.

25:12For my foot stood in uprightness;
in assemblies I will bless Thee, Lord.

26:1Of David, before being anointed.
The Lord is my light and my Savior; whom will I fear?
The Lord is the protector of my life; of whom will I be afraid?

26:2When those doing evil approached me to eat my flesh,
those who afflict me and my enemies,
they grew weak and fell.

26:3Even if an army draws up against me, my heart will not fear;
even if war rises against me, in this I hope.

26:4One thing I asked from the Lord; this I will seek:
that I may dwell in the Lord’s house all the days of my life,
that I may behold the Lord’s loveliness
and visit His temple.

26:7Hear, Lord, my voice with which I cried;
have mercy on me and hear me.

26:8My heart said unto Thee, “My face sought Thee.”
Thy face, Lord, I will seek.

26:9Do not turn Thy face away from me;
do not turn aside in anger from Thy servant.
Become my helper; do not reject me
or abandon me, God my Savior.

26:10For my father and my mother abandoned me,
but the Lord took me to Himself.

26:11Give me instruction in Thy way, Lord,
and guide me on an upright path because of my enemies.
26:13I believe that I will see the Lord’s good things in the land of the living.

27:1Of David.
To Thee, Lord, I cried;
my God, do not keep silence toward me,
lest Thou keep silence toward me
and I become like those descending into a pit.

27:2Hear the voice of my petition as I petition Thee,
as I lift my hands toward Thy holy temple.

27:3Do not drag my soul away together with sinners,
and do not destroy me together with those working injustice,
who speak peace with their neighbors
while evils are in their hearts.

27:5Because they did not understand the Lord’s works
or the works of His hands,
Thou wilt pull them down and certainly not build them up.

27:6Blessed be the Lord,
because He heard the voice of my petition.

27:8The Lord is the stronghold of His people
and the protector of the salvations of His anointed.

27:9Save Thy people and bless Thine inheritance;
shepherd them and lift them up for ever.

28:2Bring to the Lord glory for His name;
bow down to the Lord in His holy courtyard.

28:4The Lord’s voice is in strength;
the Lord’s voice is in magnificence.

28:5The voice of the Lord, who crushes cedars;
and the Lord will crush Lebanon’s cedars,

28:6and He will grind them fine—Lebanon like the calf—
and the beloved like a young one-horned animal.
28:7The voice of the Lord, who cleaves a flame of fire.

28:8The voice of the Lord, who shakes the wilderness;
and the Lord will shake the wilderness of Kadesh.

28:10The Lord will settle the flood,
and the Lord sits as King for ever.

28:11The Lord will give strength to His people;
the Lord will bless His people with peace.
29:1For the end. A psalm of a song for the dedication of the house. Of David.

29:2I will exalt Thee, Lord, for Thou tookest me up
and didst not gladden my enemies over me.

29:3Lord my God, I cried out unto Thee,
and Thou didst heal me.

29:4Lord, Thou broughtest my soul up from Hades;
Thou didst save me from those descending into a pit.

29:5Sing praise to the Lord, His holy ones,
and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness,

29:6because anger is in His wrath,
and life in His will;
weeping will lodge in the evening,
and exultation comes toward morning.

29:7But I said in my prosperity,
“I will certainly never be shaken.”

29:8Lord, in Thy will Thou didst supply strength to my beauty;
but Thou didst turn Thy face away, and I became troubled.

29:9To Thee, Lord, I will cry,
and to my God I will make my petition:

29:10“What benefit is there in my blood,
in my descending into corruption?
Will dust give thanks unto Thee,
or announce Thy truth?”

29:11The Lord heard and had mercy on me;
the Lord became my helper.

29:12Thou didst turn my lament into dancing for me;
Thou didst tear open my sackcloth and gird me with gladness,

29:13so that my glory may sing praise unto Thee,
and I may certainly not be pierced with grief.
Lord my God, I will thank Thee for ever.
30:1For the end. A psalm of David, of alarm.

30:2In Thee, Lord, I hoped; may I never be put to shame;
in Thy righteousness rescue me and bring me out.

30:4For Thou art my stronghold and my refuge,
and for Thy name’s sake Thou wilt guide me and nourish me.

30:5Thou wilt bring me out of this trap they hid for me,
for Thou art my protector.

30:6Into Thy hands I will entrust my spirit;
Thou didst redeem me, Lord, God of truth.

30:7Thou didst hate those who guard vanities to no purpose;
but I hoped in the Lord.

30:9and didst not enclose me in an enemy’s hands;
Thou didst set my feet in a spacious place.

30:11For my life failed in pain
and my years in groaning;
my strength grew weak in poverty,
and my bones were troubled.

30:12Beyond all my enemies I became a reproach,
and greatly so to my neighbors,
and a fear to my acquaintances;
those who watched me outside fled from me.

30:13I was forgotten from the heart like a dead person;
I became like a lost vessel.

30:15But I hoped in Thee, Lord;
I said, “Thou art my God.”

30:17Make Thy face shine upon Thy servant;
save me in Thy mercy.

30:18Lord, may I not be put to shame, for I called upon Thee;
may the ungodly be ashamed and brought down to Hades.

30:19Let deceitful lips become speechless,
those that speak lawlessness against the righteous
in arrogance and contempt.

30:20How great is the multitude of Thy kindness, Lord,
which Thou didst conceal for those who fear Thee,
which Thou didst accomplish for those who hope in Thee
before the sons of men!

30:21Thou wilt hide them in the hiding place of Thy presence from human turmoil;
Thou wilt shelter them in a tent from the contradiction of tongues.

30:22Blessed be the Lord,
because He made His mercy wonderful in an enclosed city.

30:23But I said in my alarm,
“So I have been cast away from before Thine eyes.”
For this reason Thou heardest the voice of my petition when I cried unto Thee.

30:24Love the Lord, all His holy ones,
because the Lord seeks truths
and repays those who act with abundant arrogance.

30:25Act courageously, and let your heart be strong,
all who hope in the Lord.

31:1Of David. Of understanding.
Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven
and whose sins are covered.

31:2Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will certainly not reckon,
and in whose mouth there is no deceit.

31:3Because I kept silent, my bones grew old
from my crying out all day long.

31:4For day and night Thy hand weighed heavily upon me;
I was turned to misery when a thorn became lodged. Diapsalma.

31:5I made my sin known,
and I did not cover my lawlessness.
I said, “I will confess my lawlessness against myself to the Lord,”
and Thou forgavest the impiety of my sin. Diapsalma.

31:6For this every holy one will pray unto Thee at a fitting time;
yet in a flood of many waters they will not approach him.

31:7Thou art my refuge from the affliction surrounding me;
my exultation, redeem me from those who have encircled me. Diapsalma.

31:8I will give you understanding and instruct you in this way in which you will go;
I will fix my eyes upon you.

31:10Many are the scourges of the sinner,
but mercy will surround the one who hopes in the Lord.

31:11Rejoice in the Lord and exult, righteous ones;
boast, all upright in heart.

32:2Give thanks to the Lord with the lyre;
make music to Him with a ten-stringed psaltery.

32:3Sing Him a new song;
make music well with a shout of triumph.

32:4For the Lord’s word is upright,
and all His works are in faithfulness.

32:5He loves mercy and judgment;
the earth is full of the Lord’s mercy.

32:6By the Lord’s word the heavens were established,
and by the spirit of His mouth all their power.

32:7He gathers the sea’s waters like a wineskin;
He places the deeps in storehouses.

32:8Let all the earth fear the Lord;
let all who inhabit the world be shaken before Him.

32:9For He spoke, and they came to be;
He commanded, and they were created.

32:11But the Lord’s counsel remains for ever,
the plans of His heart from generation to generation.

32:12Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord,
the people He chose as an inheritance for Himself.

32:13From heaven the Lord looked down;
He saw all the sons of men.

32:14From His prepared dwelling place He looked
upon all who inhabit the earth.

32:15He formed their hearts individually;
He understands all their deeds.

32:16A king is not saved through a great force,
and a giant will not be saved by the abundance of his strength.

32:17A horse is false for salvation,
and by the abundance of its power it will not be saved.

32:18Behold, the Lord’s eyes are upon those who fear Him,
those who hope in His mercy,

32:19to rescue their souls from death
and nourish them in famine.

32:20Our soul waits for the Lord,
for He is our helper and defender.

32:21For our heart will rejoice in Him,
and we have hoped in His holy name.

32:22May Thy mercy, Lord, be upon us,
just as we have hoped in Thee.

33:1Of David, when he altered his face before Abimelech,
who dismissed him, and he went away.

33:2I will bless the Lord at every time;
His praise is continually in my mouth.

33:3My soul will be praised in the Lord;
let the meek hear and rejoice.

33:4Magnify the Lord with me;
let us exalt His name together.

33:5I sought the Lord, and He heard me;
from all my sojourns He rescued me.

33:6Approach Him and be enlightened,
and your faces will certainly not be put to shame.

33:7This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him;
from all his afflictions He saved him.

33:8An angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear Him
and will rescue them.

33:9Taste and see that the Lord is kind;
blessed is the man who hopes in Him.

33:10Fear the Lord, His holy ones,
for there is no deficiency for those who fear Him.

33:11Rich people became poor and hungry,
but those who seek the Lord will not lack any good thing. Diapsalma.

33:12Come, children, listen to me;
I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

33:13Who is the person who desires life,
who loves to see good days?

33:14Stop your tongue from evil
and your lips from speaking deceit.

33:15Turn aside from evil and do good;
seek peace and pursue it.

33:16The Lord’s eyes are upon the righteous,
and His ears toward their supplication.

33:17But the Lord’s face is against those who do evil,
to destroy their remembrance from the earth.

33:18The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them;
from all their afflictions He rescued them.

33:19The Lord is near to the brokenhearted,
and He will save the humble in spirit.

33:20Many are the afflictions of the righteous,
and He will rescue them from them all.

33:21The Lord guards all their bones;
not one of them will be shattered.

33:22The death of sinners is evil,
and those who hate the righteous will incur guilt.

33:23The Lord will redeem the souls of His servants,
and none of those who hope in Him will incur guilt.

34:2Take hold of weapon and shield,
and rise to my aid.

34:3Draw the sword and close the way against those pursuing me;
say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”

34:4Let those who seek my soul be ashamed and abashed;
let those devising evils for me turn backward and be put to shame.

34:5Let them become like dust before the wind,
with an angel of the Lord pressing them out.

34:6Let their way become darkness and a slippery path,
with an angel of the Lord pursuing them.

34:7For without cause they hid for me the destruction of their trap;
without purpose they reproached my soul.

34:9But my soul will exult in the Lord;
it will delight in His salvation.

34:10All my bones will say,
“Lord, who is like Thee,
rescuing the poor from the hand of those stronger than he is,
and the poor and needy from those plundering him?”

34:11Unjust witnesses rose up;
they questioned me about what I did not know.

34:12They repaid me evils for good things,
and childlessness to my soul.

34:14As for a neighbor, as for our brother, so I sought to please;
like one mourning and downcast, so I humbled myself.

34:16They tested me and mocked me with mockery;
they gnashed their teeth at me.

34:17Lord, when wilt Thou look upon this?
Restore my soul from their wickedness,
my only life from lions.

34:18I will thank Thee, Lord, in a great assembly;
among a weighty people I will praise Thee.

34:19Let those unjustly hostile to me not rejoice over me,
those who hate me without cause and signal with their eyes.

34:20For to me they spoke peaceful things,
but in anger they devised deceits.

34:21They opened their mouth wide against me;
they said, “Well done! Well done! Our eyes have seen!”

34:22Thou hast seen, Lord; do not remain silent.
Lord, do not depart from me.

34:23Awake, Lord, and attend to my judgment,
my God and my Lord, to my case.

34:24Judge me according to Thy righteousness, Lord my God;
let them not rejoice over me.

34:25Let them not say in their hearts, “Well done! Well done for our soul!”
Nor let them say, “We have swallowed him.”

34:26May those rejoicing at my troubles be ashamed and abashed together;
let those boasting against me wear shame and humiliation.

34:28My tongue will meditate on Thy righteousness,
on Thy praise all day long.
35:1For the end. Of the Lord’s servant, of David.

35:2The lawless person speaks within himself of sinning;
there is no fear of God before his eyes.

35:3For he acted deceitfully in his sight,
as to finding his lawlessness and hating it.

35:4The words of his mouth are lawlessness and deceit;
he was unwilling to understand so as to do good.

35:6Lord, Thy mercy is in heaven,
and Thy truth reaches the clouds.

35:8How Thou hast multiplied Thy mercy, God!
The sons of men will hope beneath the shelter of Thy wings.

35:9They will be intoxicated from the richness of Thy house;
Thou wilt give them the torrent of Thy delight to drink.

35:10For with Thee is a fountain of life;
in Thy light we will see light.

35:11Extend Thy mercy to those who know Thee,
and Thy righteousness to the upright in heart.

35:12Let a foot of arrogance not come against me;
let a hand of sinners not shake me.

35:13There the workers of lawlessness fell;
they were expelled and will certainly not be able to stand.

36:1Of David.
Do not be provoked to envy by those doing evil,
nor envy those committing lawlessness.

36:2For like grass they will quickly dry up,
and like green plants they will quickly fall away.

36:3Hope in the Lord and show kindness;
settle in the land, and you will be pastured on its wealth.

36:4Delight yourself in the Lord,
and He will give you the requests of your heart.

36:5Reveal your way to the Lord;
hope in Him, and He will act.

36:6He will bring out your righteousness like light,
and your judgment like noon.

36:8Cease from anger and abandon wrath;
do not be provoked to envy so as to act wickedly.

36:9For those doing evil will be destroyed,
but those who wait for the Lord will inherit the land.

36:10A little longer, and the sinner will certainly not exist;
you will seek his place and certainly not find it.

36:11But the meek will inherit the land
and delight themselves in abundant peace.

36:12The sinner will watch the righteous closely
and gnash his teeth at him.

36:13But the Lord will laugh him to scorn,
for He foresees that his day will come.

36:14The sinners drew a sword and stretched their bow,
to cast down the poor and needy,
to slaughter the upright in heart.

36:15May their sword enter their own heart,
and may their bows be shattered.

36:16Better is a little for the righteous
than the great wealth of sinners.

36:17For the arms of sinners will be shattered,
but the Lord sustains the righteous.

36:18The Lord knows the ways of the blameless,
and their inheritance will last for ever.

36:19They will not be put to shame in an evil time,
and in days of famine they will be filled.

36:21The sinner borrows and will not repay,
but the righteous person has compassion and gives.

36:22For those blessing him will inherit the land,
but those cursing him will be destroyed.

36:23A person’s steps are directed by the Lord,
and He will desire his way.

36:24When he falls, he will not be dashed down,
for the Lord supports his hand.

36:25I was young and indeed have grown old,
and I have not seen a righteous person abandoned
or his offspring seeking loaves.

36:26All day long he shows mercy and lends,
and his offspring will be a blessing.

36:27Turn aside from evil and do good,
and dwell for age upon age.

36:28For the Lord loves judgment
and will not abandon His holy ones;
they will be guarded for ever.
But the lawless will be driven out,
and the offspring of the ungodly will be destroyed.

36:29But the righteous will inherit the land
and dwell upon it for age upon age.

36:30The mouth of the righteous will meditate on wisdom,
and his tongue will speak judgment.

36:31The law of his God is in his heart,
and his steps will not be tripped up.

36:32The sinner observes the righteous
and seeks to put him to death.

36:33But the Lord will certainly not abandon him into his hands,
nor condemn him when he comes to judgment with him.

36:35I saw an ungodly person raised high
and lifting himself like the cedars of Lebanon.

36:36I passed by, and behold, he was gone;
I sought him, but his place could not be found.

36:37Guard innocence and look upon uprightness,
for a peaceful person has a remnant.

36:38But the lawless will be destroyed together;
the remnants of the ungodly will be destroyed.

36:39But the salvation of the righteous is from the Lord,
and He is their defender in a time of affliction.
37:1A psalm of David, for remembrance concerning the Sabbath.

37:2Lord, do not rebuke me in Thy fury,
nor discipline me in Thine anger.

37:3For Thine arrows became lodged in me,
and Thou didst press Thy hand upon me.

37:4There is no healing in my flesh because of Thine anger;
there is no peace for my bones because of my sins.

37:5For my lawless deeds rose above my head;
like a heavy load they weighed upon me.

37:6My bruises stank and rotted
because of my foolishness.

37:7I suffered misery and was bent down completely;
all day long I walked about downcast.

37:8For my loins were filled with mockings,
and there is no healing in my flesh.

37:9I was afflicted and humbled exceedingly;
I roared from the groaning of my heart.

37:10Lord, all my desire is before Thee,
and my groaning was not hidden from Thee.

37:11My heart was troubled; my strength abandoned me;
and the light of my eyes—even that is not with me.

37:12My friends and neighbors approached and stood opposite me,
and those nearest me stood far away.

37:14But like a deaf person I did not hear,
like one unable to speak who does not open his mouth.

37:15I became like a person who does not hear
and has no rebukes in his mouth.

37:16For I hoped in Thee, Lord;
Thou wilt hear, Lord my God.

37:17For I said, “Let my enemies never rejoice over me!”
When my feet were shaken, they boasted against me.

37:18For I am ready for scourges,
and my pain is continually before me.

37:19For I will announce my lawlessness
and be concerned about my sin.

37:20But my enemies live and have become stronger than I,
and those hating me unjustly have multiplied.

37:21Those repaying evils for good things slandered me
because I pursued righteousness,
and they cast me, the beloved, away like an abhorred corpse.

37:22Do not abandon me, Lord;
my God, do not depart from me.

37:23Attend to my aid,
Lord of my salvation.
38:1For the end. For Jeduthun. A song of David.

38:2I said, “I will guard my ways so as not to sin with my tongue.”
I placed a guard upon my mouth
when the sinner stood against me.

38:3I became mute and was humbled and kept silent from good things,
and my pain was renewed.

38:4My heart grew hot within me,
and in my meditation a fire will be kindled.
I spoke with my tongue:

38:5“Make known to me, Lord, my limit
and the number of my days, what it is,
so that I may know what I lack.

38:6Behold, Thou madest my days handbreadths,
and my existence is as nothing before Thee.
Yet all things are vanity—every living person. Diapsalma.

38:8And now, what is my expectation? Is it not the Lord?
And my existence comes from Thee.

38:9Rescue me from all my lawless deeds;
Thou hast given me as a reproach to a fool.

38:10I became mute and did not open my mouth,
because Thou art the One who made me.

38:11Remove Thy scourges from me;
from the strength of Thy hand I wasted away.

38:12With rebukes for lawlessness Thou didst discipline a person
and melt his soul like a spider.
Yet every person is troubled in vain. Diapsalma.

38:13Hear my prayer, Lord, and give ear to my supplication;
do not remain silent at my tears.
For I am a sojourner with Thee
and a temporary resident like all my fathers.

38:14Give me relief, that I may be refreshed,
before I depart and no longer exist.”
39:1For the end. A psalm of David.

39:2I waited patiently for the Lord;
He attended to me and heard my supplication.

39:3He brought me up from a pit of misery
and from muddy slime;
He set my feet upon a rock
and directed my steps.

39:4He put a new song into my mouth,
a hymn to our God.
Many will see and fear
and hope in the Lord.

39:5Blessed is the man whose hope is the Lord’s name
and who has not looked toward vanities and false frenzies.

39:6Many are the wonders Thou hast done, Lord my God,
and in Thy purposes there is no one who can be compared with Thee.
I announced and spoke;
they multiplied beyond number.

39:7Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire,
but ears Thou didst prepare for me.
Burnt offering and an offering for sin Thou didst not request.

39:8Then I said, “Behold, I have come;
in the scroll of the book it is written concerning me.

39:9I desired to do Thy will, my God,
and Thy law within my belly.”

39:12But Thou, Lord, do not put Thy compassions far from me;
Thy mercy and Thy truth have continually sustained me.

39:13For evils without number surrounded me;
my lawless deeds overtook me, and I could not see.
They multiplied beyond the hairs of my head,
and my heart abandoned me.

39:14Be pleased, Lord, to rescue me;
Lord, attend to helping me.

39:15May those seeking my soul to remove it be ashamed and abashed together;
may those desiring evils for me turn backward and be abashed.

39:16Let those saying to me, “Well done! Well done!”
receive their shame immediately.
40:1For the end. A psalm of David.

40:2Blessed is the one who understands the poor and needy;
in an evil day the Lord will rescue him.

40:3May the Lord guard him, keep him alive and bless him in the land;
may He not hand him over into his enemy’s hands.

40:4May the Lord help him upon his bed of pain;
Thou didst turn all his bed in his weakness.

40:5I said, “Lord, have mercy on me;
heal my soul, for I sinned against Thee.”

40:6My enemies spoke evils against me:
“When will he die and his name perish?”

40:8Together all my enemies whispered against me;
against me they devised evils for me.

40:9They laid a lawless word against me:
“Can it be that the one lying down will not rise again?”

40:10For even the man of my peace, in whom I hoped,

41:1For the end. For understanding, of the sons of Korah.

41:2As the deer longs for springs of water,
so my soul longs for Thee, God.

41:3My soul thirsted for the living God.
When will I come and appear before God’s face?

41:4My tears became my bread day and night,
while it is said to me every day, “Where is your God?”

41:5These things I remembered and poured out my soul within me:
for I will pass through the place of a wonderful tent to God’s house,
with a voice of exultation and thanksgiving,
a celebrating sound.

41:6Why are you deeply grieved, soul, and why do you disturb me?
Hope in God, for I will thank Him:
my God is the salvation of my face.

41:8Deep calls upon deep at the sound of Thy waterfalls;
all Thy billows and Thy waves passed over me.

41:9By day the Lord will command His mercy,
and at night a song is with me,
a prayer to the God of my life.

41:10I will say to God, “Thou art my supporter; why hast Thou forgotten me?
Why do I walk downcast while my enemy oppresses me?”

41:11As they crushed my bones, those afflicting me reproached me,
saying to me every day, “Where is your God?”

41:12Why are you deeply grieved, soul, and why do you disturb me?
Hope in God, for I will thank Him:
my God is the salvation of my face.

42:2For Thou, God, art my strength; why didst Thou thrust me away?
And why do I walk downcast while my enemy oppresses me?

42:5Why are you deeply grieved, soul, and why do you disturb me?
Hope in God, for I will thank Him:
my God is the salvation of my face.
43:1For the end. A psalm of the sons of Korah, for understanding.

43:3Thy hand destroyed nations, and Thou didst plant our fathers;
Thou didst afflict peoples and cast them out.

43:4For they did not inherit the land by their sword,
and their arm did not save them,
but Thy right hand, Thine arm and the light of Thy face,
because Thou didst delight in them.

43:5Thou Thyself art my King and my God,
who commands the salvations of Jacob.

43:6Through Thee we will gore our enemies,
and through Thy name we will bring to nothing those rising against us.

43:7For I will not hope in my bow,
and my sword will not save me.

43:8For Thou didst save us from those afflicting us
and put those who hate us to shame.

43:9In God we will be praised all day long,
and in Thy name we will give thanks for ever. Diapsalma.

43:10But now Thou didst thrust us away and put us to shame,
and Thou wilt not go out with our forces.

43:11Thou didst turn us backward before our enemies,
and those who hate us plundered for themselves.

43:12Thou gavest us like sheep for eating
and didst scatter us among the nations.

43:13Thou soldest Thy people without a price,
and there was no abundance in their exchange.

43:14Thou madest us a reproach to our neighbors,
scorn and ridicule to those around us.

43:15Thou madest us a parable among the nations,
a shaking of the head among the peoples.

43:16All day long my humiliation is before me,
and the shame of my face covered me,

43:17at the voice of one reproaching and speaking abusively,
at the presence of an enemy and pursuer.

43:18All these things came upon us, and we did not forget Thee
or act unjustly in Thy covenant.

43:19And our heart did not withdraw backward,
but Thou didst turn our paths away from Thy way.

43:20For Thou didst humble us in a place of affliction,
and death’s shadow covered us.

43:21If we forgot our God’s name,
and if we spread our hands toward a foreign god,

43:22will God not search these things out?
For He knows the heart’s hidden things.

43:23For Thy sake we are put to death all day long;
we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.

43:24Awake! Why dost Thou sleep, Lord?
Arise, and do not thrust us away completely.

43:25Why dost Thou turn Thy face away
and forget our poverty and affliction?

43:26For our soul was humbled to the dust;
our belly clung to the earth.

43:27Arise, Lord; help us,
and redeem us for the sake of Thy name.

44:1For the end, concerning those who will be changed.
Of the sons of Korah, for understanding. A song concerning the beloved.

44:4Gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one,
in your fairness and your beauty,

44:6Your arrows are sharpened, mighty one—peoples will fall beneath you—
in the heart of the king’s enemies.

44:7Your throne, God, is for age upon age;
a rod of uprightness is the rod of your kingdom.

44:9Myrrh, stacte and cassia come from your garments,

44:11Listen, daughter, look and incline your ear,

because he is your lord.

44:13And daughters of Tyre will bow down to him with gifts;

44:14All the glory of the king’s daughter is within;
she is arrayed in gold-fringed, varied embroidery.

44:15Virgins behind her will be brought to the king;
her companions will be brought unto you.

45:1For the end. Concerning the sons of Korah. A psalm concerning hidden things.

45:2Our God is refuge and strength,
a helper in the afflictions that have greatly overtaken us.

45:3Therefore we will not fear when the earth is disturbed
and mountains are displaced into the hearts of seas.

45:4Their waters roared and were disturbed;
the mountains were disturbed at his might. Diapsalma.

45:5The river’s rushing streams gladden God’s city;
the Most High sanctified His dwelling.

45:6God is in her midst; she will not be shaken;
God will help her toward morning.

45:7Nations were disturbed; kingdoms bent;
He gave His voice; the earth was shaken.

45:8The Lord of powers is with us;
Jacob’s God is our supporter. Diapsalma.

45:9Come, see the Lord’s works,
the wonders He has set upon the earth.

45:10Bringing wars to an end as far as the earth’s limits,

45:12The Lord of powers is with us;
Jacob’s God is our supporter.
46:1For the end. A psalm concerning the sons of Korah.

46:2All nations, clap your hands;
shout to God with a voice of exultation.

46:3For the Lord Most High is fearsome,
a great King over all the earth.

46:4He subjected peoples to us
and nations beneath our feet.

46:5He chose His inheritance for us,
the beauty of Jacob, which He loved. Diapsalma.

46:6God ascended with a shout of triumph,
the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.

46:7Make music to our God, make music;
make music to our King, make music.

make music with understanding.

47:1A psalm of song for the sons of Korah, on the second day of the week.

47:2Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised
in our God’s city, His holy mountain,

47:3taking good root for the exultation of all the earth.
Zion’s mountains, the sides of the north,
the city of the great King.

they came together.

they were troubled and shaken.

there were pangs like a woman giving birth.

in the midst of Thy sanctuary.

47:12Let Mount Zion rejoice;
let Judea’s daughters exult because of Thy judgments, Lord.

recount in her towers,

so that you may tell another generation.
48:1For the end. A psalm of the sons of Korah.

48:2Hear these things, all nations;
give ear, all who inhabit the world,

48:3both the earthborn and the sons of men,
rich and poor together.

48:4My mouth will speak wisdom,
and my heart’s meditation understanding.

48:5I will incline my ear to a parable;
with a psaltery I will open my riddle.

48:6Why do I fear in an evil day?
The lawlessness of my heel will surround me.

48:7Those trusting in their strength
and boasting in the abundance of their wealth,

48:8A brother does not redeem; will a person redeem?
He will not give God his atonement price

48:10And he ceased for ever and will live to the end,
for he will not see corruption when he sees wise people dying.

48:11The foolish and senseless will perish together

48:13A person, though in honor, did not understand;
he was compared to senseless beasts and made like them.

48:14This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them,
and afterward they will take delight with their mouth. Diapsalma.

48:15Like sheep they were placed in Hades; death shepherds them.

and their help will grow old in Hades, away from their glory.

48:16But God will redeem my soul from Hades’ hand
when He receives me. Diapsalma.

48:17Do not fear when a person grows rich
and when the glory of his house increases.

48:18For when he dies he will not take everything,
nor will his glory descend with him.

48:19For his soul will be blessed during his lifetime;
he will thank you when you do good to him.

48:20He will enter as far as the generation of his fathers;
he will never see light.

48:21A person, though in honor, did not understand;
he was compared to senseless beasts and made like them.

49:1A psalm of Asaph.
The God of gods, the Lord, spoke and summoned the earth
from the sun’s risings to its settings.

49:2From Zion comes the splendor of His beauty;
God will come manifestly,

49:4He will summon heaven above
and the earth, to judge His people.

49:5Gather His holy ones to Him,
those who establish His covenant over sacrifices.

49:6The heavens will announce His righteousness,
for God is judge. Diapsalma.

49:8I will not rebuke you concerning your sacrifices;
your burnt offerings are continually before Me.

49:9I will not receive calves from your house
or young goats from your flocks.

49:10For all the forest’s wild animals are Mine,
beasts on the mountains and cattle.

49:11I know all the birds of heaven,
and the field’s beauty is with Me.

49:12If I become hungry, I will certainly not tell you,
for the inhabited world and its fullness are Mine.

49:13Will I eat bulls’ flesh
or drink goats’ blood?

49:14Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God
and pay your vows to the Most High.

49:15Call on Me in the day of affliction;
I will rescue you, and you will glorify Me.” Diapsalma.

and take up My covenant through your mouth?

49:17But you hated instruction
and cast My words behind you.

49:18If you saw a thief, you would run along with him,
and you would place your portion with adulterers.

49:19Your mouth multiplied wickedness,
and your tongue was weaving deception.

49:20Sitting, you would speak against your brother,
and against your mother’s son you would place a stumbling block.

49:22Understand these things, you who forget God,
lest He seize you and there be no rescuer.

49:23A sacrifice of praise will glorify Me,
and there is a way by which I will show him God’s salvation.”
50:1For the end. A psalm of David,

50:2when Nathan the prophet came to him,
when he had gone in to Bathsheba.

50:3Have mercy on me, God, according to Thy great mercy,
and according to the abundance of Thy compassions blot out my lawless deed.

50:4Wash me more and more from my lawlessness,
and cleanse me from my sin.

50:5For I know my lawlessness,
and my sin is continually before me.

50:6Against Thee alone I sinned
and did evil before Thee,
so that Thou mayest be justified in Thy words
and prevail when Thou art judged.

50:7For behold, I was conceived in lawless deeds,
and in sins my mother conceived me.

50:8For behold, Thou didst love truth;
Thou madest known to me the unseen and hidden things of Thy wisdom.

50:9Thou wilt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be cleansed;
Thou wilt wash me, and I will be whitened beyond snow.

50:10Thou wilt make me hear exultation and gladness;
humbled bones will exult.

50:11Turn Thy face away from my sins,
and blot out all my lawless deeds.

50:12Create in me a clean heart, O God,
and renew an upright spirit in my inward parts.

50:13Do not cast me away from Thy face,
and do not remove Thy holy Spirit from me.

50:14Restore to me the exultation of Thy salvation,
and strengthen me with a governing spirit.

50:15I will teach the lawless Thy ways,
and the ungodly will turn back unto Thee.

50:16Rescue me from bloodshed, God, God of my salvation;
my tongue will exult in Thy righteousness.

50:17Lord, Thou wilt open my lips,
and my mouth will announce Thy praise.

50:18For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would have given it;
Thou wilt not delight in burnt offerings.

50:19A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit;
a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.

50:20Do good to Zion, Lord, in Thy good pleasure,
and let Jerusalem’s walls be built.
51:1For the end. Of understanding, of David,

51:2when Doeg the Idumean came and reported to Saul,
and said to him, “David came to Abimelech’s house.”

51:3Why do you boast in wickedness, mighty one,
in lawlessness all day long?

51:4Your tongue devised injustice;
like a sharpened razor you worked deceit.

51:5You loved wickedness more than goodness,
injustice more than speaking righteousness. Diapsalma.

51:6You loved every word of drowning,
a deceitful tongue.

51:8The righteous will see and fear;
they will laugh at him and say:

51:9“Look at the person who did not make God his helper,
but hoped in the abundance of his wealth
and became strong in his vanity.”

51:11I will thank Thee for ever, because Thou didst act,
and I will wait for Thy name,
because it is kind before Thy holy ones.
52:1For the end. Concerning Maeleth. Of understanding, of David.

52:3God bent down from heaven toward the sons of men,
to see whether anyone understands or seeks God.

52:4All turned aside; together they became useless;
there is no one doing good, not a single one.

52:5Will all who work lawlessness not learn?
Those eating my people like the eating of bread did not call on God.

52:6There they will fear greatly where there was no fear,
for God scattered the bones of people-pleasers.
They were put to shame, for God despised them.

52:7Who will give Israel’s salvation from Zion?
When the Lord turns back His people’s captivity,
Jacob will exult and Israel will rejoice.
53:1For the end. Among hymns. Of understanding, of David.
53:2When the Ziphites came and said to Saul, “Behold, is David not hidden among us?”

53:3God, save me by Thy name,
and judge me by Thy power.

53:4God, hear my prayer;
give ear to the words of my mouth.

53:6For behold, God helps me,
and the Lord is the supporter of my soul.

53:7He will turn the evils back upon my enemies;
in Thy truth, utterly destroy them.

53:8I will sacrifice unto Thee willingly;
I will give thanks to Thy name, Lord, for it is good.

53:9For Thou didst rescue me from every affliction,
and my eye has looked upon my enemies.
54:1For the end. Among hymns. Of understanding, of David.

54:2Give ear, God, to my prayer,
and do not overlook my petition.

54:3Attend to me and hear me.
I was grieved in my meditation and troubled

54:4by an enemy’s voice and a sinner’s affliction,
for they turned lawlessness upon me
and harbored anger against me.

54:5My heart was troubled within me,
and dread of death fell upon me.

54:6Fear and trembling came upon me,
and darkness covered me.

54:7I said, “Who will give me wings like a dove’s,
so that I may fly away and rest?”

54:8Behold, I went far away in flight
and lodged in the wilderness. Diapsalma.

54:9I waited for the one saving me
from faintheartedness and tempest.

54:10Drown them, Lord, and divide their tongues,
for I saw lawlessness and contradiction in the city.

54:11Day and night it will circle it upon its walls;
lawlessness and toil are within it, and injustice,
54:12and interest-taking and deceit did not depart from its squares.

54:13For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have endured it;
and if the one hating me had boasted against me, I would have hidden from him.

54:14But you, a man of like soul,
my leader and my acquaintance,

54:15you who made food sweet together with me:
in God’s house we walked in concord.

54:16Let death come upon them,
and let them descend alive into Hades,
for wicked things are in their sojournings, within them.

54:17But I cried to God,
and the Lord heard me.

54:18Evening, morning and noon I will recount;
I will proclaim, and He will hear my voice.

54:19He will redeem my soul in peace from those drawing near me,
for among many they were with me.

54:20God will hear and humble them,
He who exists before the ages. Diapsalma.
For they have no exchange,
and they did not fear God.

54:21He stretched out his hand in making repayment;
they profaned his covenant.

54:22They were divided by the anger of his face,
and his heart drew near;
his words became softer than oil,
yet they are missiles.

54:23Cast your care upon the Lord, and He will nourish you;
He will never give the righteous a shaking.
55:1For the end. Concerning the people far removed from the holy ones. Of David, for an inscription on a pillar, when the foreigners seized him in Gath.

55:2Have mercy on me, Lord, for a man trampled me;
fighting all day, he afflicted me.

55:3My enemies trampled me all day,
for many are those fighting me from a height.

55:4By day I will fear,
but I will hope in Thee.

55:5In God I will praise my words all day.
In God I have hoped; I will not fear.
What will flesh do to me?

55:6All day they detested my words;
all their thoughts against me are for evil.

55:8For nothing Thou wilt save them;
in anger Thou wilt bring down peoples, God.

55:9I declared my life unto Thee; Thou
didst set my tears before Thee, as also in Thy promise.

55:10My enemies will turn backward on whatever day I call upon Thee.
Behold, I know that Thou art my God.

55:11In God I will praise an utterance;
in the Lord I will praise a word.

55:12In God I have hoped; I will not fear.
What will a human being do to me?
55:13Within me, God, are the vows of praise that I will pay unto Thee,

55:14because Thou didst rescue my soul from death
and my feet from slipping,
that I may be pleasing before God in the light of the living.
56:1For the end. Do not destroy. Of David, for an inscription on a pillar, when he escaped from Saul’s presence into the cave.

56:2Have mercy on me, God, have mercy on me,
for my soul has trusted in Thee;
in the shadow of Thy wings I will hope
until lawlessness passes.

56:3I will cry to God Most High,
to God who has done good to me.

56:5and rescued my soul from among young lions.
I lay down troubled.
Sons of men—their teeth are a weapon and arrows,
and their tongue a sharp sword.

56:6Be exalted above the heavens, God,
and Thy glory above all the earth.

56:7They prepared a trap for my feet
and bowed my soul down;
they dug a pit before me
and fell into it. Diapsalma.

56:8My heart is ready, God; my heart is ready.
I will sing and make music.

56:9Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and lyre!
I will awake at dawn.

56:10I will give thanks unto Thee among peoples, Lord;
I will make music unto Thee among nations,

56:11for Thy mercy was magnified to the heavens,
and Thy truth to the clouds.

56:12Be exalted above the heavens, God,
and Thy glory above all the earth.
57:1For the end. Do not destroy. Of David, for an inscription on a pillar.

57:2Do you then truly speak righteousness?
Do you judge uprightly, sons of men?

57:3For indeed in your heart you work lawless deeds on earth;
your hands weave injustice together.

57:4Sinners were estranged from the womb;
from the belly they went astray and spoke lies.

57:5Their fury is in the likeness of a serpent,
like that of a deaf asp that stops up its ears,

57:6which will not hear the voice of enchanters,
or a spell being cast by a wise person.

57:7God shattered their teeth in their mouth;
the Lord crushed the lions’ grinders.

57:8They will be reduced to nothing like water passing away;
He will stretch His bow until they grow weak.

57:9Like wax that melted, they will be taken away;
fire fell, and they did not see the sun.

57:10Before your thorns understand the buckthorn,
as though alive, as in anger, He will swallow you.

57:11A righteous person will rejoice when he sees vengeance upon the ungodly;
he will wash his hands in the sinner’s blood.

57:12A human being will say, “Then there is indeed fruit for the righteous;
then there is God judging them on earth.”
58:1For the end. Do not destroy. Of David, for an inscription on a pillar, when Saul sent and watched his house to put him to death.

and redeem me from those rising against me.

and save me from men of bloodshed.

God will show me what concerns my enemies.

58:14in the anger of consummation, and they shall certainly not exist;

58:15They will return toward evening, hunger like a dog,
and circle a city.

58:16They will be scattered in search of food;
and if they are not filled, they will grumble.

for Thou becamest my supporter

60:1For the end. Among hymns. Of David.

60:2Hear my petition, God;
attend to my prayer.

Thou didst raise me upon a rock,

60:4Thou didst guide me, for Thou becamest my hope,
a tower of strength before the enemy.

his years until the day of generation upon generation.

who will seek out his mercy and truth?

61:1For the end. Concerning Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

61:2Will my soul not submit to God?
For from Him is my salvation.

61:3For He is my God and my Savior,
my supporter; I shall certainly not be shaken any further.

61:4How long do you attack a human being?
All of you murder,
as against a leaning wall and a fence thrust down.

61:6Nevertheless submit to God, my soul,
for my endurance is from Him.

61:7For He is my God and my Savior,
my supporter; I shall certainly not migrate away.

61:8Upon God rest my salvation and my glory;
the God of my help—and my hope is upon God.

61:11Do not hope in injustice or long for plunder;
if wealth flows, do not attach your heart.

61:13that power belongs to God, and mercy unto Thee, Lord,
