62:1A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judea.

62:2God, my God, toward Thee I rise at dawn;
my soul thirsted for Thee.
How greatly my flesh longs for Thee
in a desert, trackless and waterless land!

62:3So I was seen by Thee in the holy place,
to see Thy power and Thy glory.

62:4For Thy mercy is better than lives;
my lips will praise Thee.

62:5So I will bless Thee in my life;
in Thy name I will lift my hands.

62:6May my soul be filled as with fat and richness,
and my mouth will praise with lips of exultation.

62:7If I remembered Thee upon my bed,
in the dawn hours I meditated upon Thee.

62:8For Thou becamest my helper,
and in the shelter of Thy wings I will exult.

62:9My soul clung behind Thee;
Thy right hand supported me.

62:10But they sought my soul in vain;
they will enter the lowest places of the earth.

62:11They will be handed over into the hands of a sword;
they will be portions for foxes.
63:1For the end. A psalm of David.

63:2Hear my voice as I petition, God;
take my soul out from fear of the enemy.

63:3Thou didst shelter me from a conspiracy of evildoers,
from a multitude working lawlessness,

63:4who sharpened their tongues like a sword
and stretched their bow—a bitter deed—

63:5to shoot down a blameless one in hidden places;
suddenly they will shoot him down and will not fear.

63:8and God will be exalted.
Their blows became an infants’ arrow,

63:9and their tongues grew powerless against them.
All who saw them were troubled,

63:10and every human being feared.
They announced God’s works
and understood His acts.

63:11A righteous person will rejoice in the Lord and hope in Him,
and all the upright in heart will be praised.
64:1For the end. A psalm of David, a song. Of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, from the account of the sojourn, when they were about to depart.

64:2A hymn befits Thee, God, in Zion,
and unto Thee a vow will be paid in Jerusalem.

64:3Hear my prayer;
unto Thee all flesh will come.

64:4Words of lawless deeds overpowered us,
and Thou wilt make atonement for our impieties.

64:6Hear us, God our Savior,
the hope of all earth’s ends
and of those far away at sea,

64:7who prepares mountains in His strength,
girded with power;

64:8who troubles the sea’s hollow,
the sounds of its waves.
The nations will be troubled,

64:9and those dwelling at the ends will fear Thy signs;
Thou wilt gladden the departures of morning and evening.

64:12Thou wilt bless the crown of the year of Thy kindness,
and Thy plains will be filled with richness.

64:13The beautiful places of the wilderness will grow rich,
and the hills will gird themselves with exultation.

65:1For the end. A song of a psalm. Of resurrection.
Raise a shout to God, all the earth!

65:2Make music, then, to His name;
give glory to His praise.

65:3Say to God, “How fearsome are Thy works!
Through the abundance of Thy power,
Thine enemies will lie unto Thee.

65:4Let all the earth bow unto Thee and make music unto Thee;
let them make music to Thy name.” Diapsalma.

65:5Come and see God’s works,
fearsome in His counsels concerning the sons of men,

65:8Bless our God, nations,
and cause the sound of His praise to be heard,

65:9He who set my soul in life
and did not give my feet over to shaking.

65:10For Thou didst test us, God;
Thou didst try us by fire as silver is tried by fire.

65:11Thou broughtest us into the trap;
Thou didst place afflictions upon our back.

65:13I will enter Thy house with whole burnt offerings;
I will pay Thee my vows,

65:14which my lips declared
and my mouth spoke in my affliction.

65:16Come, hear, all who fear God,
and I will recount all that He did for my soul.

65:17I cried to Him with my mouth
and lifted up beneath my tongue:

65:18“If I was regarding injustice in my heart,
let the Lord not hear.”

65:19For this reason God heard me;
He attended to the sound of my petition.

65:20Blessed is God,
who did not turn away my prayer
or His mercy from me.
66:1For the end. Among hymns. A psalm of a song.

66:2May God have compassion on us and bless us;
may He make His face shine upon us. Diapsalma.

66:3That Thy way may be known on earth,
Thy salvation among all nations.

66:4Let peoples give thanks unto Thee, God;
let all peoples give thanks unto Thee.

66:5Let nations rejoice and exult,
for Thou wilt judge peoples in uprightness
and guide nations upon the earth. Diapsalma.

66:6Let peoples give thanks unto Thee, God;
let all peoples give thanks unto Thee.

66:7The earth gave its fruit;
may God, our God, bless us.

66:8May God bless us,
and let all earth’s ends fear Him.
67:1For the end. Of David, a psalm of a song.

67:2Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered,
and let those hating Him flee from His presence.

67:4Let the righteous rejoice and exult before God;
let them delight in gladness.

67:5Sing to God; make music to His name.
Make a road for Him who rides upon the west—Lord is His name—
and exult before Him.
They will be troubled before Him,

67:6the Father of orphans and judge of widows,
God in His holy place.

67:7God settles those of one disposition in a house,
leading out the fettered with courage,
likewise the rebellious who dwell in tombs.

67:8God, when Thou wentest out before Thy people,
when Thou didst pass through the wilderness—Diapsalma—

67:9the earth shook, and indeed the heavens dripped
before God—this Sinai—
before the God of Israel.

67:10Thou wilt set apart willing rain, God, for Thine inheritance;
it grew weak, but Thou didst restore it.

67:11Thy living creatures dwell in it;
in Thy kindness Thou didst prepare for the poor, God.
67:12The Lord will give an utterance to those announcing good news with great power,

67:13the king of the powers of the beloved,
and for the beauty of the house to divide spoils.

67:14If you sleep between the allotted portions—
a dove’s wings plated with silver,
and its back in the green sheen of gold. Diapsalma.

67:15When the Heavenly One distinguishes kings upon it,
they will be covered with snow in Selmon.

67:16A mountain of God, a rich mountain;
a curdled mountain, a rich mountain.

67:17Why do you suppose, curdled mountains,
that this is the mountain in which God was pleased to dwell?
For indeed the Lord will dwell to the end.

67:19Thou didst ascend on high; Thou tookest captivity captive;
Thou didst receive gifts among humankind,
and indeed the disobedient, to establish a dwelling.
Blessed is the Lord God.

67:20Blessed is the Lord day by day;
the God of our salvations will prosper our way. Diapsalma.

67:21Our God is a God of saving,
and to the Lord, the Lord, belong the exits of death.

67:22Nevertheless God will crush His enemies’ heads,
the crown of hair of those walking in their offenses.

67:23The Lord said, “I will return from Bashan;
I will return in the depths of the sea,

67:24so that your foot may be dipped in blood,
and the tongue of your dogs from enemies, from him.”

67:25Thy processions were seen, God,
the processions of my God, the King in the holy place.

67:26Rulers went first, closely followed by musicians,
amid young women beating tambourines.

67:27In assemblies bless God,
the Lord, from Israel’s springs.

67:29Command Thy power, God;
strengthen, God, this which Thou didst accomplish for us.

67:30From Thy sanctuary over Jerusalem,
kings will bring Thee gifts.

67:31Rebuke the beasts of the reed,
the assembly of bulls among the heifers of peoples,
so that those tested by silver may not be shut out;
scatter nations that desire wars.

67:32Envoys will come from Egypt;
Ethiopia will hasten its hand toward God.

67:33Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God;
make music to the Lord. Diapsalma.

67:34Make music to God, who rides upon the heaven of heaven toward the east;
behold, He will give with His voice a voice of power.
68:1For the end. Concerning those who will be changed. Of David.

68:2Save me, God,
for waters have entered as far as my soul.

68:3I was stuck in the mud of the depth, with no firm ground;
I entered the sea’s depths, and a tempest drowned me.

68:4I grew weary crying out; my throat became hoarse;
my eyes failed from hoping in my God.

68:6God, Thou knewest my folly,
and my offenses were not concealed from Thee.

68:7May those waiting for Thee not be ashamed because of me,
Lord, Lord of powers;
may those seeking Thee not be embarrassed because of me,
God of Israel,

68:8for on Thine account I endured reproach;
embarrassment covered my face.

68:9I became estranged from my brothers
and a foreigner to my mother’s sons,

68:10for zeal for Thy house devoured me,
and the reproaches of those reproaching Thee fell upon me.

68:11I bowed my soul down in fasting,
and it became a reproach to me.

68:12I made sackcloth my garment,
and became a proverb to them.

68:13Those sitting in the gate talked against me,
and wine-drinkers sang about me.

68:15Save me from clay so that I may not become stuck;
may I be rescued from those hating me and from the depth of waters.

68:17Hear me, Lord, for Thy mercy is kind;
according to Thine abundant compassions, look upon me.

68:18Do not turn Thy face away from Thy servant;
for I am afflicted, hear me quickly.

68:19Attend to my soul and redeem it;
because of my enemies, rescue me.

68:20For Thou knowest my reproach, shame and embarrassment;
all those afflicting me are before Thee.

68:22They gave gall for my food,
and for my thirst made me drink sour wine.

68:23Let their table before them become a trap,
a repayment and a stumbling block.

68:24Let their eyes be darkened so they cannot see,
and bend their back down continually.

68:25Pour Thine anger upon them;
may the fury of Thine anger seize them.

68:26Let their homestead become deserted;
let no one dwell in their dwellings.

68:27For they persecuted the one Thou didst strike,
and added to the pain of Thy wounded.

68:28Add lawlessness to their lawlessness,
and let them not enter Thy righteousness.

68:29Let them be erased from the book of the living,
and let them not be written with the righteous.

68:30I am poor and in pain,
and the salvation of Thy presence, God, supported me.

68:31I will praise God’s name with a song
and magnify Him in praise,

68:32and it will please God more than a young calf
bringing forth horns and hoofs.

68:33Let the poor see and rejoice;
seek God, and your soul will live,

68:34for the Lord heard the needy
and did not despise His bound ones.

68:35Let the heavens and earth praise Him,
the sea and everything creeping in them.

68:37His servants’ offspring will possess it,
and those loving His name will dwell in it.
69:1For the end. Of David. For remembrance,

69:2for the Lord to save me.
God, attend to my help!

69:3May those seeking my soul be ashamed and confounded;
may those wishing me evil turn backward and be disgraced.

69:4May those saying to me, “Well! Well!”
turn back immediately in shame.

70:2In Thy righteousness rescue me and bring me out;
bend Thine ear toward me and save me.

70:3Become for me a defending God
and a fortified place to save me,
for Thou art my firm support and my refuge.

70:4My God, rescue me from a sinner’s hand,
from the hand of one acting lawlessly and unjustly.

70:5For Thou art my endurance, Lord;
the Lord is my hope from my youth.

70:7I became like a portent to the many,
and Thou art a mighty helper.

70:8Let my mouth be filled with praise,
so that I may sing of Thy glory,
Thy majesty all day.

70:9Do not cast me away at the time of old age;
when my strength fails, do not forsake me.

70:10For my enemies spoke to me,
and those watching my soul plotted together,

70:11saying, “God has forsaken him!
Pursue him and overtake him,
for there is no rescuer!”

70:12God, do not go far from me;
my God, attend to my help!

70:13Let those slandering my soul be ashamed and fail;
let those seeking evil for me wrap themselves in shame and confusion.

70:14But I will always hope,
and add to all Thy praise.

70:15My mouth will proclaim Thy righteousness,
Thy salvation all day,
for I did not know literary learning.

70:16I will enter in the Lord’s power;
Lord, I will remember Thy righteousness alone.

70:17Thou didst teach me, God, from my youth,
and until now I will announce Thy wonders.

70:18And until old age and advanced years, God, do not forsake me,
until I announce Thine arm to the whole coming generation,
Thy power and Thy righteousness—

70:19God, up to the highest—what great things Thou hast done!
God, who is like Thee?

70:20How many troubles, many and grievous, Thou didst show me!
And turning back, Thou madest me live,
and from the depths of the earth Thou broughtest me up again.

70:21Thou didst increase Thy greatness,
and turning back, didst comfort me,
and from the depths of the earth Thou broughtest me up again.

70:23My lips will exult when I sing unto Thee,
and my soul, which Thou didst redeem.

70:24And my tongue too will meditate on Thy righteousness all day,
when those seeking evil for me become ashamed and confounded.

71:1For Solomon.
God, give Thy judgment to the king,
and Thy righteousness to the king’s son,

71:2to judge Thy people in righteousness,
and Thy poor in justice.

71:3Let the mountains take up peace for Thy people,
and the hills in righteousness.

71:4He will judge the poor of the people,
and save the children of the needy,
and humble the false accuser,

71:5and he will endure alongside the sun,
and before the moon, through generations of generations.

71:6And he will descend like rain upon a fleece,
and like drops dripping upon the earth.

71:7Righteousness will arise in his days,
and abundant peace until the moon is taken away.

71:8And he will rule from sea to sea,
and from the river to the ends of the inhabited world.

71:9Ethiopians will fall before him,
and his enemies will lick dust.

71:10kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts;
kings of the Arabians and Saba will bring gifts.

71:11And all kings will bow before him;
all nations will serve him.

71:12For he rescued a poor person from a powerful man’s hand,
and a needy person who had no helper.

71:13He will spare the poor and needy,
and save the souls of the needy.

71:14From interest-taking and injustice he will redeem their souls,
and their name is honored before him.

71:18Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel,
who alone does wonders!
71:20The hymns of David son of Jesse have ended.

72:1A psalm of Asaph.
How good God is to Israel,
to those upright in heart!

72:2But my feet were almost shaken;
my steps were nearly poured out.

72:3For I envied the lawless,
beholding sinners’ peace,

72:4for there is no refusal at their death,
and firmness in their scourging.

72:5They are not in human toils,
and they will not be scourged with humans.

72:6Therefore arrogance seized them;
they wrapped themselves in their injustice and ungodliness.

72:7Their injustice will come out as though from fat;
they passed into a disposition of heart.

72:8They devised and spoke in wickedness;
they spoke injustice against the height.

72:9They set their mouth toward heaven,
and their tongue passed over the earth.

72:10Therefore my people will return here,
and full days will be found for them.

72:11And they said, “How did God know?
And is there knowledge in the Most High?”

72:12Behold, these are sinners, and they prosper;
for the age they took possession of wealth.

72:13And I said, “Then in vain I made my heart righteous
and washed my hands among the innocent;

72:14and I became scourged all day,
and my rebuke comes in the mornings.”

72:15If I were saying, “I will recount it thus,”
behold, I would have broken faith with the generation of Thy sons.

72:16And I undertook to understand this;
it is toil before me,

72:17until I enter God’s sanctuary
and understand their last things.

72:18Nevertheless, because of their deceits Thou didst set things for them;
Thou didst cast them down when they were lifted up.

72:19How they became desolate suddenly!
They failed; they perished through their lawlessness.

72:20Like the dream of someone awakening,
Lord, in Thy city Thou wilt count their image as nothing.

72:21For my heart was set ablaze,
and my kidneys were altered,

72:22and I was counted as nothing and did not understand;
I became beastlike beside Thee.

72:23And I am continually with Thee;
Thou didst grasp my right hand.

72:24In Thy counsel Thou didst guide me,
and with glory Thou didst receive me.

72:25For what is there for me in heaven?
And what did I desire from Thee upon the earth?

72:26My heart and my flesh failed;
the God of my heart and my portion is God for ever.

72:27For behold, those distancing themselves from Thee will perish;
Thou didst destroy everyone who goes whoring away from Thee.

72:28But for me, clinging to God is good,
to set my hope in the Lord,
to proclaim all Thy praises
in the gates of the daughter of Zion.

73:1Of understanding. Of Asaph.
Why, God, didst Thou reject to the end?
Why was Thy wrath angry against the sheep of Thy pasture?

73:3Raise Thy hands against their arrogance to the end,
for all the evil the enemy did in Thy holy places.

73:4And those hating Thee boasted within Thy feast;
they set their signs as signs, and did not understand.
73:5As though into the entrance above,

73:6as in a forest of trees, with axes they cut out her doors;
together with axe and stone-cutting tool they tore her down.

73:7They burned Thy sanctuary with fire;
they profaned the tent of Thy name to the ground.

73:8Their kindred said in their hearts together,
“Come, let us burn all God’s feasts from the earth!”

73:10How long, God, will the enemy reproach?
Will the adversary provoke Thy name to the end?

73:11Why dost Thou turn away Thy hand
and Thy right hand from within Thy bosom to the end?

73:12But God is our King before the age;
He worked salvation in the midst of the earth.

73:13Thou didst strengthen the sea by Thy power;
Thou didst crush the dragons’ heads upon the water.

73:14Thou didst crush the dragon’s heads;
Thou gavest him as food to the Ethiopian peoples.

73:15Thou didst break open springs and torrents;
Thou didst dry up rivers of Etham.

73:16Thine is the day, and Thine is the night;
Thou didst fashion light and the sun.

73:17Thou madest all the earth’s boundaries;
summer and spring—Thou didst shape them.

73:18Remember this: an enemy reproached the Lord,
and a foolish people provoked Thy name.

73:19Do not hand over to wild beasts a soul acknowledging Thee;
do not forget Thy needy ones’ souls to the end.

73:20Look upon Thy covenant,
for the darkened ones of the earth were filled with houses of lawlessness.

73:21Let a humbled person not turn back disgraced;
the poor and needy will praise Thy name.

73:22Arise, God, judge Thy case;
remember the reproaches against Thee by a fool all day.

73:23Do not forget Thy suppliants’ voice;
the arrogance of those hating Thee ascended continually toward Thee.

74:1For the end. Do not destroy.
A psalm of Asaph, of song.

74:2We will acknowledge Thee, God;
we will acknowledge and call upon Thy name.

74:3I will recount all Thy wonders when I take an appointed time;
I will judge uprightness.

74:5I said to those acting lawlessly, “Do not act lawlessly,”
and to those sinning, “Do not raise a horn;

74:6do not lift your horn on high;
do not speak injustice against God.”

74:7For neither from the goings-out nor from the settings,
nor from desert mountains,

74:8for God is judge:
He humbles this one and raises that one.

74:10But I will exult for ever;
I will sing to the God of Jacob.

74:11And I will break together all sinners’ horns;
and the righteous person’s horns will be raised.

75:1For the end, among hymns.
A psalm of Asaph; a song concerning the Assyrian.

75:2God is known in Judea;
His name is great in Israel.

75:3His place came to be in peace,
and His dwelling in Zion.

75:4There He crushed the bows’ powers,
weapon and sword and war.
Diapsalma.

75:5Thou givest light wondrously
from everlasting mountains.

75:7At Thy rebuke, God of Jacob,
those mounted on horses grew drowsy.

75:8Thou art fearsome, and who will withstand Thee?
From that time is Thy wrath.

75:9From heaven Thou didst cause judgment to be heard;
the earth feared and grew quiet,

75:10when God arose for judgment,
to save all the earth’s meek.
Diapsalma.

75:11For human thought will acknowledge Thee,
and the remainder of thought will keep a feast for Thee.

75:12Make vows and repay the Lord your God;
all around Him will bring gifts

75:13to the Fearsome One, who takes away rulers’ spirits,
who is fearsome among the earth’s kings.

76:1For the end, concerning Jeduthun.
Of Asaph. A psalm.

76:2With my voice I cried to the Lord,
with my voice to God, and He attended to me.

76:5My eyes anticipated the watches;
I was troubled and did not speak.

76:6I considered ancient days,
and remembered everlasting years and meditated.

76:7At night I spoke at length with my heart,
and my spirit kept searching.

76:8“Will the Lord reject for the ages,
and not again take pleasure?

76:9Or will He cut off His mercy to the end,
from generation to generation?

76:10Or will God forget to show pity,
or hold His compassions shut in His wrath?”
Diapsalma.

76:11And I said, “Now I have begun;
this is the change of the Most High’s right hand.”

76:12I remembered the Lord’s works,
for I will remember Thy wonders from the beginning,

76:13and meditate on all Thy works,
and speak at length about Thy practices.

76:14God, Thy way is in the Holy One;
what god is great like our God?

76:15Thou art the God who does wonders;
Thou madest Thy power known among the peoples.

76:16With Thine arm Thou didst redeem Thy people,
the sons of Jacob and Joseph.
Diapsalma.

76:18The clouds gave voice,
for Thine arrows too pass through.

76:20Thy way is in the sea,
and Thy paths in many waters,
and Thy tracks will not be known.

76:21Thou didst guide Thy people like sheep
by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

77:2I will open my mouth in parables;
I will utter riddles from the beginning,

77:3whatever we heard and knew,
and our fathers recounted to us,

77:4it was not hidden from their children for another generation,
as we announce the Lord’s praises,
His mighty acts and the wonders He did.

77:5And He raised a testimony in Jacob
and set a law in Israel,
whatever He commanded our fathers
to make known to their sons,

77:7so that they may set their hope upon God
and not forget God’s works,
and seek out His commandments,

77:8so that they may not become like their fathers,
a crooked and embittering generation,
a generation that did not direct its heart,
whose spirit was not faithful with God.

77:9The sons of Ephraim, drawing and shooting bows,
turned back on the day of war.

77:10They did not keep God’s covenant
and were unwilling to walk in His law,

77:11and forgot His benefits
and the wonders He showed them,

77:12the wonders He did before their fathers,
in Egypt’s land, in the plain of Tanis.

77:13He tore the sea apart and led them through;
He stood the waters like a skin-bag,

77:14and guided them with a cloud by day,
and all night with the light of fire.

77:15He split a rock in the wilderness
and gave them drink as in a great deep,

77:16and brought water out of a rock
and made waters descend like rivers.

77:17And they continued still to sin against Him;
they embittered the Most High in a waterless place,

77:18and put God to the test in their hearts,
asking food for their souls,

77:19and spoke against God and said,
“Surely God cannot prepare a table in a wilderness?

77:20Since He struck a rock and waters flowed,
and torrents were flooded,
surely He cannot also give bread
or prepare a table for His people?”

77:22because they did not believe in God
nor hope in His salvation.

77:23And He commanded the clouds above
and opened heaven’s doors,

77:24and rained manna for them to eat,
and gave them heaven’s bread.

77:25A man ate angels’ bread;
He sent them food supplies to fullness.

77:26He moved the south wind from heaven,
and brought the southwest wind by His power,

77:27and rained flesh upon them like dust,
and winged birds like the sands of seas,

77:28and they fell within their camp,
around their tents,

77:29and they ate and were filled exceedingly,
and He brought them their desire.

77:30They were not deprived of their desire.
While their food was still in their mouth,

77:31then God’s wrath rose against them,
and He killed among their fat ones,
and entangled Israel’s chosen men.

77:32In all these things they sinned still
and did not believe in His wonders,

77:33and their days failed in futility,
and their years with haste.

77:34Whenever He killed them, they sought Him;
and they returned and rose early toward God,

77:35and remembered that God is their helper,
and God Most High is their redeemer.

77:36And they deceived Him with their mouth,
and lied to Him with their tongue,

77:37but their heart was not upright with Him,
nor were they faithful in His covenant.

77:38But He is compassionate;
He will make atonement for their sins and not destroy,
and will turn back His wrath again and again,
and will not kindle all His anger.

77:39And He remembered that they are flesh,
a spirit going away and not returning.

77:40How often they embittered Him in the wilderness
and angered Him in a waterless land!

77:41And they turned again and tested God,
and provoked the Holy One of Israel.

77:42They did not remember His hand,
the day He redeemed them from an oppressor’s hand,

77:43how He set His signs in Egypt
and His portents in the plain of Tanis,

77:44and turned their rivers into blood,
and their rain-waters, so that they might not drink.

77:45He sent a dog-fly among them, and it devoured them,
and a frog, and it destroyed them.

77:46And He gave their fruit to mildew,
and their labors to the locust.

77:47He killed their vine with hail,
and their sycamores with frost.

77:48And He handed their cattle over to hail,
and their possessions to fire.

77:49He sent upon them the anger of His wrath,
wrath, anger and affliction,
a mission through evil angels.

77:51and struck every firstborn in Egypt,
the firstfruits of their labors in Ham’s tents.

77:52And He led His people away like sheep,
and brought them up like a flock in the wilderness,

77:53and guided them in hope, and they did not grow cowardly;
and the sea covered their enemies.

77:54And He brought them into the boundary of His sanctuary,
this mountain which His right hand acquired,

77:55and expelled nations from before them,
and assigned them by a cord of inheritance,
and settled Israel’s tribes in their tents.

77:56And they tested and embittered God Most High,
and did not keep His testimonies,

77:57and turned back and broke faith just like their fathers,
and changed into a crooked bow,

77:58and angered Him with their hills,
and provoked Him to jealousy with their carvings.

77:59God heard and disregarded,
and counted Israel as utterly nothing,

77:60and rejected Shiloh’s tent,
His dwelling, where He encamped among humans.

77:61And He handed their strength over to captivity,
and their beauty into an enemy’s hands,

77:62and confined His people to the sword,
and disregarded His inheritance.

77:63Fire devoured their young men,
and their virgins were not mourned.

77:64Their priests fell by the sword,
and their widows will not be wept for.

77:65And the Lord awoke like one sleeping,
like a powerful man heavy with wine,

77:66and struck His enemies backward;
He gave them everlasting reproach.

77:67And He rejected Joseph’s dwelling,
and did not choose Ephraim’s tribe.

77:68And He chose Judah’s tribe,
Mount Zion, which He loved,

77:69and built His sanctuary like that of one-horned beasts;
in the earth He founded it for ever.

77:70And He chose David His servant,
and took him up from the flocks of sheep;

77:71from behind the ewes giving birth He took him,
to shepherd Jacob His people
and Israel His inheritance.

77:72And he shepherded them in his heart’s innocence,
and guided them with his hands’ understanding.

78:2They made the dead bodies of Thy servants
food for the birds of heaven,
the flesh of Thy holy ones for the beasts of the earth.

78:3They poured out their blood like water
around Jerusalem,
and there was no one to bury them.

78:4We became a reproach to our neighbors,
sneering and ridicule to those around us.

78:5How long, Lord? Wilt Thou be angry to the end?
Will Thy jealousy blaze like fire?

78:6Pour out Thy wrath upon nations that do not know Thee,
and upon kingdoms that did not call on Thy name,

78:7for they devoured Jacob
and made his place desolate.

78:9Help us, God our Savior.
For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us,
and be propitious toward our sins
for Thy name’s sake,

78:10lest the nations say, “Where is their God?”
And let vengeance for the poured-out blood of Thy servants
be known among the nations before our eyes.

78:12Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom
their insult with which they insulted Thee, Lord.

79:1For the end; concerning those who will be changed.
A testimony for Asaph; a psalm concerning the Assyrian.

79:3Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh,
rouse Thy dominion,
and come to save us.

79:4God, turn us back;
make Thy face shine, and we shall be saved.

79:5Lord, God of powers,
how long art Thou angry at the prayer of Thy servant,

79:6wilt Thou feed us bread of tears
and give us tears to drink by measure?

79:7Thou madest us an object of contradiction for our neighbors,
and our enemies sneered at us.

79:9Thou didst transplant a vine from Egypt;
Thou didst cast out nations and plant her.

79:10Thou madest a road before her
and didst plant her roots,
and the land was filled.

79:11Her shadow covered mountains,
and her climbing branches covered God’s cedars.

79:12She stretched her branches as far as the sea,
and her offshoots as far as the River.

79:13Why didst Thou tear down her fence,
so that all who pass along the road harvest her?

79:14A pig from the woodland ravaged her,
and a solitary wild beast grazed her down.

79:16and restore her whom Thy right hand planted,
and upon the son of man whom Thou didst strengthen for Thyself.

79:17Burned with fire and dug up—
at the rebuke of Thy face they will perish.

79:18Let Thy hand come upon the man of Thy right hand
and upon the son of man whom Thou didst strengthen for Thyself.

79:19And we shall certainly not depart from Thee;
Thou wilt give us life, and we will call on Thy name.

79:20Lord, God of powers, turn us back;
make Thy face shine, and we shall be saved.
80:1For the end; concerning the winepresses. A psalm for Asaph.

80:2Exult in God our helper;
raise a shout to the God of Jacob.

80:3Take up a psalm and sound the tambourine,
a delightful psaltery together with a lyre.

80:4Sound the trumpet at the new moon,
on the conspicuous day of our feast.

80:5For it is an ordinance for Israel
and a judgment of the God of Jacob.

80:7He removed his back from burdens;
his hands served at the basket.

80:9Hear, My people, and I solemnly testify to you;
Israel, if you listen to Me,

80:10There shall be no new god among you,
nor shall you bow down to a foreign god.

80:11For I am the Lord your God,
who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.

80:12And My people did not listen to My voice,
and Israel did not pay attention to Me.

80:13So I sent them away according to the practices of their hearts;
they will walk in their practices.

80:14If My people had listened to Me,
if Israel had walked in My ways,

80:15in no time I would have humbled their enemies
and laid My hand upon those who afflict them.

80:16The Lord’s enemies lied to Him,
and their appointed time will be for ever.

80:17And He fed them with the finest wheat,
and with honey from rock He satisfied them.

81:1A psalm for Asaph.
God stood in an assembly of gods,
and in their midst He judges gods:

81:2“How long do you judge injustice
and favor sinners?
Diapsalma.

81:3Judge for the fatherless and the poor;
vindicate the lowly and the needy.

81:4Deliver the needy and the poor;
rescue them from the hand of a sinner.”

81:6“I said, ‘You are gods,
and all sons of the Most High.’

81:7But you die like human beings,
and fall like one of the rulers.”

81:8Rise, God, judge the earth,
for Thou wilt take inheritance among all the nations.
82:1A song of a psalm for Asaph.

82:2God, who will be likened unto Thee?
Do not be silent or remain quiet, God.

82:3For behold, Thine enemies made an uproar,
and those who hate Thee lifted their head.

82:4Against Thy people they cunningly devised a plan,
and they took counsel against Thy holy ones.

82:5They said, “Come, let us destroy them from being a nation,
and Israel’s name shall certainly be remembered no more.”

82:6For they took counsel together in concord;
against Thee they made a covenant—

82:7the dwellings of the Idumeans, and the Ishmaelites,
Moab and the Hagarenes,

82:8Gebal and Ammon and Amalek,
and foreigners with those who inhabit Tyre.

82:10Do to them as to Midian and Sisera,
as with Jabin at the torrent Kishon,

82:11they were destroyed at En-dor
and became like dung for the earth.

82:12Make their rulers like Oreb and Zeeb,
and Zebah and Zalmunna—all their rulers,

82:13who said, “Let us inherit for ourselves
the sanctuary of God.”

82:14My God, make them like a wheel,
like straw before the wind.

82:15Like fire that will burn through a woodland,
as though a flame should burn up mountains,

82:16so Thou wilt pursue them with Thy storm
and trouble them in Thy wrath.

82:17Fill their faces with dishonor,
and they will seek Thy name, Lord.

82:18Let them be ashamed and troubled for an age of an age;
let them be abashed and perish,

82:19and let them know that Thy name is Lord;
Thou alone art Most High over all the earth.

83:1For the end; concerning the winepresses.
A psalm for the sons of Korah.

83:2How beloved are Thy dwellings,
Lord of powers!

83:3My soul longs and faints for the courts of the Lord;
my heart and my flesh exulted in the living God.

83:4For even a sparrow found itself a house,
and a turtledove a nest for herself, where she will place her young—
Thine altars, Lord of powers,
my King and my God.

83:6Blessed is the man whose support is from Thee, Lord;
he arranged ascents in his heart,

83:7in the valley of weeping, toward a place which he appointed;
for the lawgiver will also give blessings.

83:8They will go from power to power;
the God of gods will appear in Zion.

83:10Look, God our defender;
look upon the face of Thine anointed.

83:13Lord of powers,
blessed is the person who hopes in Thee.

84:1For the end.
A psalm for the sons of Korah.

84:2Thou tookest pleasure in Thy land, Lord;
Thou didst turn back Jacob’s captivity.

84:4Thou didst stop all Thy wrath;
Thou didst turn away from the anger of Thy fury.

84:5Turn us back, God of our deliverances,
and turn Thy fury away from us.

84:6Surely Thou wilt not be angry with us for ever,
or extend Thy wrath from generation to generation?

84:7God, Thou wilt turn back and give us life,
and Thy people will rejoice in Thee.

84:8Show us Thy mercy, Lord,
and mayest Thou give us Thy salvation.

84:9I will hear what the Lord God will speak within me,
for He will speak peace upon His people
and upon His holy ones
and upon those who turn their heart toward Him.

84:10Nevertheless His salvation is near those who fear Him,
so that glory may dwell in our land.

84:11Mercy and truth met;
righteousness and peace kissed.

84:12Truth sprang up from the earth,
and righteousness looked down from heaven.

84:13For the Lord will also give goodness,
and our land will give its fruit.

84:14Righteousness will go ahead before Him
and set His footsteps on a path.

85:1A prayer for David.
Incline Thine ear, Lord, and hear me,
for I am poor and needy.

85:3Have mercy on me, Lord,
for unto Thee I will cry all day.

85:4Gladden the soul of Thy servant,
for unto Thee, Lord, I lifted my soul.

85:5For Thou, Lord, art kind and forbearing,
abundant in mercy to all who call on Thee.

85:6Give ear, Lord, to my prayer,
and attend to the voice of my petition.

85:7On the day of my affliction I cried unto Thee,
for Thou heardest me.

85:8There is none like Thee among gods, Lord,
and nothing is like Thy works.

85:9All the nations Thou madest will come
and bow down before Thee, Lord,
and glorify Thy name,

85:10for Thou art great and dost wondrous things;
Thou alone art the great God.

85:12I will give Thee thanks, Lord my God, with all my heart,
and glorify Thy name for ever,

85:13for Thy mercy toward me is great,
and Thou didst deliver my soul from lowest Hades.

85:15And Thou, Lord God, art compassionate and merciful,
long-suffering, abundant in mercy, and true.

85:17Work a sign for good with me,
and let those who hate me see and be ashamed,
for Thou, Lord, didst help and comfort me.

86:1For the sons of Korah, a psalm of a song.
Its foundations are in the holy mountains.

86:2The Lord loves the gates of Zion
more than all the dwellings of Jacob.

86:3Glorified things were spoken about you, city of God.
Diapsalma.

86:4I will remember Raab and Babylon to those who know me.
And look: foreigners and Tyre and the people of Ethiopians—
these were born there.

86:6The Lord will recount in a register of peoples
and of these rulers who were born in her.
Diapsalma.
86:7The dwelling in you is like that of all who rejoice.

87:1A song of a psalm for the sons of Korah.
For the end; concerning Maeleth, for answering.
Of understanding; of Heman the Israelite.

87:2Lord, God of my salvation,
by day I cried out, and by night before Thee.

87:3Let my prayer enter before Thee;
incline Thine ear to my petition, Lord.

87:4For my soul was filled with evils,
and my life drew near Hades.

87:6like wounded people cast down, sleeping in a grave,
whom Thou didst remember no more,
and who were thrust away from Thy hand.

87:7They put me in the lowest pit,
in dark places and in death’s shadow.

87:8Thy fury rested firmly upon me,
and Thou broughtest all Thy surges upon me.
Diapsalma.

87:11Surely Thou wilt not work wonders for the dead?
Or will physicians raise them, and will they give Thee thanks?

87:12Surely no one will recount Thy mercy in a grave
and Thy truth in destruction?

87:13Surely Thy wonders will not be known in darkness,
or Thy righteousness in a forgotten land?

87:14And I cried unto Thee, Lord,
and in the morning my prayer will reach Thee first.

87:15Why, Lord, dost Thou thrust away my soul
and turn Thy face away from me?

87:16I am poor and in toils from my youth;
but after being raised up, I was humbled and left helpless.

87:17Thy wraths passed over me,
and Thy threats utterly troubled me;

87:18they encircled me like water all day;
together they closed around me.

87:19Thou didst remove friend and neighbor far from me,
and my acquaintances because of misery.
88:1Of understanding; of Ethan the Israelite.

88:2I will sing of Thy mercies, Lord, for ever;
from generation to generation I will proclaim Thy truth with my mouth,

88:3for Thou saidst, “Mercy will be built for ever;
in the heavens Thy truth will be prepared.”

88:4“I made a covenant with My chosen ones;
I swore to David My servant:

88:5‘I will prepare your seed for ever
and build your throne from generation to generation.’”
Diapsalma.

88:6The heavens will acknowledge Thy wonders, Lord,
and Thy truth in an assembly of holy ones.

88:7For who in clouds will be equaled to the Lord,
and who among sons of God will be likened to the Lord?

88:8God is glorified in the council of holy ones,
great and fearsome above all around Him.

88:9Lord, God of powers, who is like Thee?
Thou art mighty, Lord, and Thy truth surrounds Thee.

88:10Thou rulest the sea’s might,
and Thou quietest the surge of its waves.

88:11Thou didst humble a proud one like a wounded man,
and with the arm of Thy power Thou didst scatter Thine enemies.

88:12The heavens are Thine, and the earth is Thine;
the inhabited world and its fullness—Thou didst found them.

88:13The north and seas—Thou didst create them;
Tabor and Hermon will exult in Thy name.

88:14Thine is the arm with dominion;
let Thy hand be strengthened; let Thy right hand be raised.

88:15Righteousness and judgment are the preparation of Thy throne;
mercy and truth will go ahead before Thy face.

88:16Blessed are the people who know the cry of triumph;
Lord, they will walk in the light of Thy face,

88:17and in Thy name they will exult all day,
and in Thy righteousness they will be raised up.

88:18For Thou art the boast of their power,
and by Thy favor our horn will be raised.

88:19For support belongs to the Lord,
and to the Holy One of Israel, our King.

88:21I found David My servant;
with My holy oil I anointed him,

88:22for My hand will support him,
and My arm will strengthen him.

88:23An enemy will not gain by him,
and a son of lawlessness will not go on to harm him.

88:24I will cut down his enemies before him
and put those who hate him to flight.

88:25My truth and My mercy will be with him,
and in My name his horn will be raised.

88:26I will set his hand in the sea
and his right hand in rivers.

88:27He will call on Me, ‘Thou art my Father,
my God and the supporter of my salvation.’

88:28And I will make him firstborn,
high among the kings of the earth.

88:29For ever I will keep My mercy for him,
and My covenant is faithful to him.

88:30I will establish his seed for an age of an age
and his throne like the days of heaven.

88:31If his sons abandon My law
and do not walk in My judgments,

88:32if they profane My ordinances
and do not keep My commandments,

88:33I will visit their lawless acts with a rod
and their sins with scourges;

88:34but I shall certainly not scatter My mercy away from him,
nor act unjustly in My truth,

88:35nor shall I profane My covenant,
and what goes out through My lips I shall certainly not set aside.

88:36Once I swore by My holiness:
I will not lie to David.

88:37His seed will remain for ever,
and his throne will be like the sun before Me,

88:39But Thou didst reject and treat as nothing;
Thou didst put off Thine anointed.

88:40Thou didst overturn Thy servant’s covenant;
Thou didst profane his consecrated thing to the ground.

88:41Thou didst tear down all his fences;
Thou madest his fortifications cowardice.

88:42All who travel the road plundered him;
he became a reproach to his neighbors.

88:43Thou didst raise the right hand of his enemies;
Thou didst gladden all his enemies.

88:44Thou didst turn back the help of his sword
and didst not support him in war.

88:45Thou didst remove him from purification;
Thou didst dash his throne down to the ground.

88:47How long, Lord? Wilt Thou turn away to the end?
Will Thy wrath blaze like fire?

88:48Remember what my existence is;
for surely Thou didst not create all the sons of men in vain?

88:49Who is the person who will live and not see death,
who will deliver his soul from the hand of Hades?
Diapsalma.

88:50Where are Thine ancient mercies, Lord,
which Thou didst swear to David in Thy truth?

88:51Remember, Lord, the reproach of Thy servants,
which I bore in my bosom from many nations,

88:52with which Thine enemies reproached, Lord,
with which they reproached the exchange of Thine anointed.

88:53Blessed be the Lord for ever.
May it be; may it be.

89:1A prayer of Moses, the man of God.
Lord, Thou becamest our refuge through every generation.

89:2Before the mountains came to be
and the earth and inhabited world were formed,
from age to age Thou art.

89:3Do not turn a man toward humiliation;
and Thou saidst, Return, sons of men.

89:4For a thousand years in Thine eyes
are like yesterday, which passed,
and a watch in the night.

89:5Their things counted as nothing will be years.
In the morning, like green grass, may it pass away;

89:6in the morning may it blossom and pass away;
in the evening may it fall, grow hard and dry up.

89:7For we failed in Thine anger
and were troubled in Thy wrath.

89:8Thou didst set our lawless deeds before Thee;
our age is in the light of Thy face.

89:10The days of our years—in them are seventy years,
or, with strength, eighty years;
the greater part of them is toil and pain,
for gentleness came upon us, and we shall be disciplined.

89:11Who knows the might of Thine anger,
and Thy wrath from the fear of Thee?

89:12So make known how to number Thy right hand,
and those bound in heart in wisdom.

89:13Return, Lord—how long?
Be moved concerning Thy servants.

89:14We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy,
and we exulted and rejoiced all our days.

89:15We were glad in return for the days Thou didst humble us,
the years when we saw evils.

89:16Look upon Thy servants and Thy works,
and guide their children.

89:17Let the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us,
and direct the works of our hands for us.

90:1A praise of a song, of David.
The one dwelling in the help of the Most High
will lodge in the shelter of the God of heaven.

90:2He will say to the Lord, Thou art my Helper and my refuge,
my God; I will hope in Him.

90:3For He will rescue me from the hunters’ trap
and from a disturbing word.

90:5You will not fear terror by night,
the missile flying by day,

90:6the thing passing through darkness,
the calamity and the demon of noon.

90:7A thousand will fall at your side
and ten thousand at your right hand,
but it will not come near you.

90:8You will only observe with your eyes
and see the repayment of sinners.

90:9For Thou, Lord, art my hope.
You have made the Most High your refuge.

90:10Evils will not approach you,
and a scourge will not come near your dwelling.

90:11For He will command His angels concerning you,
to guard you in all your ways.

90:12On their hands they will lift you,
lest you strike your foot against a stone.

90:13You will step on an asp and a basilisk,
and trample a lion and a dragon.

90:14Because he hoped in Me, I will rescue him;
I will shelter him, because he knew My name.

90:16With length of days I will fill him
and show him My salvation.
91:1A psalm of a song, for the Sabbath day.

91:2It is good to give thanks to the Lord
and make music to Thy name, Most High,

91:3to declare Thy mercy in the morning
and Thy truth by night,

91:4on a ten-stringed psaltery,
with song on a lyre.

91:5For Thou didst gladden me, Lord, by Thy making,
and at the works of Thy hands I will exult.

91:6How great Thy works have become, Lord;
Thy reasonings have grown very deep.

91:7A senseless man will not know,
and one without understanding will not understand these things:

91:8when sinners spring up like grass
and all who work lawlessness emerge,
it is so that they may be utterly destroyed for the age of the age.
91:9But Thou art Most High for ever, Lord.

91:10For behold, Thine enemies will perish,
and all who work lawlessness will be scattered.

91:11My horn will be raised like a one-horned creature’s,
and my old age in rich oil.

91:12My eye looked upon my enemies,
and my ear will hear of evildoers rising against me.

91:13A righteous person will blossom like a palm tree;
like the cedar in Lebanon he will multiply.

91:14Planted in the Lord’s house,
they will blossom in the courts of our God.

91:15They will still multiply in a rich old age
and be flourishing,

91:16to declare that the Lord my God is upright,
and there is no injustice in Him.

92:1For the day before the Sabbath, when the earth has been inhabited; a praise of a song, of David.
The Lord reigned, clothed Himself in comeliness;
the Lord clothed Himself in power and girded Himself.
For He established the inhabited world, which will not be shaken.

92:2Thy throne is ready from then;
Thou art from the age.

92:3The rivers lifted up, Lord;
the rivers lifted up their voices.

93:2Be exalted, Judge of the earth;
give repayment to the arrogant.

93:3How long, Lord, will sinners—
how long will sinners boast,

93:4utter and speak injustice—
will all who work lawlessness speak?

93:5They humbled Thy people, Lord,
and mistreated Thine inheritance.

93:6They killed the widow and newcomer
and murdered orphans.

93:7They said, The Lord will not see,
nor will the God of Jacob understand.

93:8Understand now, you senseless among the people;
and you fools, become wise at last.

93:9Does the One who planted the ear not hear,
or the One who formed the eye not perceive?

93:10Will the One who disciplines nations not rebuke—
the One who teaches humankind knowledge?

93:11The Lord knows human reasonings,
that they are futile.

93:12Happy the person Thou disciplinest, Lord,
whom Thou teachest from Thy law,

93:13to soothe him from evil days,
until a pit is dug for the sinner.

93:14For the Lord will not reject His people,
nor abandon His inheritance,

93:15until righteousness returns to judgment,
and all the upright in heart cling to it. Diapsalma.

93:16Who will rise for me against evildoers,
or who will stand beside me against workers of lawlessness?

93:17Had the Lord not helped me,
my soul would almost have sojourned in Hades.

93:18If I said, My foot has been shaken,
Thy mercy, Lord, helps me.

93:19Lord, amid the multitude of pains in my heart,
Thy consolations loved my soul.

93:20Will a throne of lawlessness join Thee,
one that shapes toil by command?

93:21They will hunt a righteous person’s soul
and condemn innocent blood.

93:22The Lord became my refuge,
and my God the Helper of my hope.

93:23He will repay them their lawlessness,
and according to their wickedness
the Lord our God will obliterate them.

94:2Let us come before His face with thanksgiving,
and with psalms let us shout to Him.

94:3For the Lord is a great God
and a great King above all gods.

94:4For in His hand are the earth’s ends,
and the mountain heights are His.

94:5For the sea is His, and He made it,
and His hands formed the dry land.

94:6Come, let us bow down and fall before Him,
and let us weep before the Lord who made us.

94:7For He is our God,
and we are the people of His pasture and the sheep of His hand.
Today, if you hear His voice,

94:8do not harden your hearts as in the provocation,
on the day of testing in the wilderness,

94:9where your ancestors tested,
put to the proof, and saw My works.

94:10For forty years I was vexed with that generation
and said, They always stray in heart,
and they did not know My ways,

94:11as I swore in My anger,
They shall not enter My rest.

95:2Sing to the Lord; bless His name.
Proclaim the good news of His salvation day after day.

95:3Announce His glory among the nations,
His wonders among all the peoples.

95:4For great is the Lord and greatly to be praised;
He is fearsome above all gods.

95:5For all the gods of the nations are demons,
but the Lord made the heavens.

95:6Thanksgiving and beauty are before Him;
holiness and magnificence are in His sanctuary.

95:7Bring to the Lord, families of nations;
bring to the Lord glory and honor.

95:8Bring to the Lord glory for His name;
take up sacrifices and enter His courts.

95:9Bow down to the Lord in His holy court;
let all the earth be shaken before Him.

95:10Say among the nations, “The Lord has become King!”

He will judge peoples with uprightness.

95:11Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult;
let the sea be shaken, and all that fills it.

95:12The plains will rejoice, and everything in them;
then all the trees of the woodland will exult

95:13before the Lord, for He is coming,
for He is coming to judge the earth.
He will judge the inhabited world with righteousness
and peoples with His truth.

96:2Cloud and gloom surround Him;
righteousness and judgment are the establishment of His throne.

96:3Fire will go ahead before Him
and set His enemies aflame all around.

96:4His lightning flashes shone upon the inhabited world;
the earth saw and was shaken.

96:5The mountains melted like wax before the Lord,
before the Lord of all the earth.

96:6The heavens announced His righteousness,
and all the peoples saw His glory.

96:7Let all who bow down to carved images be ashamed,
those who boast in their idols.

96:8Zion heard and rejoiced,
and the daughters of Judea exulted

96:9For Thou art the Lord, the Most High over all the earth;

96:11Light has dawned for the righteous,
and gladness for the upright in heart.

96:12Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous,
and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness.

97:1A psalm of David.
Sing to the Lord a new song, for the Lord has done wonders.
His right hand and His holy arm won salvation for Him.

before the nations He revealed His righteousness.

97:3He remembered His mercy to Jacob
and His truth to the house of Israel.
All the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God.

97:4Shout to God, all the earth;
sing and exult and make music.

with a lyre and the sound of a psalm.

shout before the King, the Lord.

97:7Let the sea be shaken, and all that fills it,
the inhabited world and those who dwell in it.

97:8Rivers will clap their hands together;
the mountains will exult,
