He sits upon the cherubim; let the earth be shaken.

98:2The Lord is great in Zion
and exalted above all the peoples.

98:3Let them give thanks to Thy great name,
for it is fearsome and holy.

98:5Exalt the Lord our God
and bow down at His footstool,
for He is holy.

98:6Moses and Aaron were among His priests,
and Samuel among those who call on His name.
They called upon the Lord, and He heard them,

98:7He spoke to them in a pillar of cloud.
They kept His testimonies
and the ordinances He gave them.

98:9Exalt the Lord our God
and bow down toward His holy mountain,
for holy is the Lord our God.

99:1A psalm for thanksgiving.
Shout to the Lord, all the earth.

99:2Serve the Lord with gladness;
enter before Him with exultation.

99:4Enter His gates with thanksgiving,
His courts with hymns.
Give thanks to Him; praise His name.

99:5For the Lord is kind; His mercy is for ever,
and His truth through generation after generation.

100:1Of David. A psalm.
I will sing mercy and judgment unto Thee, Lord;

100:2I will make music and understand in a blameless way.
When wilt Thou come to me?
I used to walk in innocence of my heart within my house.

100:3I did not set a lawless matter before my eyes;
I hated those who commit transgressions.

100:4A crooked heart did not cling to me;
when the evil one turned away from me, I did not know him.

100:5The one secretly speaking against his neighbor I used to drive away;
with a proud eye and an insatiable heart, with that one I did not eat.

100:6My eyes were on the faithful of the land, that they might sit with me;
the one walking in a blameless way used to minister to me.

100:7One practicing arrogance did not dwell within my house;
one speaking unjust things did not prosper before my eyes.

100:8In the mornings I used to kill all the sinners of the land,
to destroy from the Lord’s city all who practice lawlessness.
101:1A prayer of a poor person when he becomes despondent and pours out his petition before the Lord.

101:2Hear my prayer, Lord,
and let my cry come unto Thee.

101:4For my days vanished like smoke,
and my bones were scorched like kindling.

101:5My heart was struck like grass and dried up,
for I forgot to eat my bread.

101:6From the sound of my groaning,
my bone clung to my flesh.

101:7I became like a wilderness pelican;
I became like a night raven on a house site.

101:8I stayed awake and became
like a little bird alone on a roof.

101:9All day my enemies reproached me,
and those praising me swore against me.

101:10For I ate ashes like bread
and mixed my drink with weeping,

101:11because of Thine anger and wrath,
for after lifting me up Thou didst dash me down.

101:12My days bent like a shadow,
and I dried up like grass.

101:13But Thou, Lord, remainest for ever,
and Thy memorial is from generation to generation.

101:14Thou wilt arise and have compassion on Zion,
for it is time to have compassion on her; the time has come.

101:15For Thy servants took pleasure in her stones
and will have compassion on her dust.

101:16Nations will fear the Lord’s name,
and all the kings of the earth Thy glory,

101:17for the Lord will build Zion
and will appear in His glory.

101:18He looked upon the prayer of the lowly
and did not treat their petition as nothing.

101:19Let this be written for another generation,
and the people being created will praise the Lord,

101:20for He leaned out from His holy height;
the Lord looked from heaven upon the earth,

101:21to hear the groaning of those in bonds,
to release the sons of those put to death,

101:22to announce the Lord’s name in Zion
and His praise in Jerusalem,

101:23when peoples are gathered together,
and kingdoms, to serve the Lord.

101:24He answered him in the way of his strength:
Tell me the fewness of my days.

101:25Do not take me up at the halfway point of my days;
Thy years extend through a generation of generations.

101:26At the beginning Thou, Lord, didst found the earth,
and the heavens are works of Thy hands.

101:28But Thou art the same,
and Thy years will not fail.

101:29The children of Thy servants will make their dwelling,
and their offspring will be established for ever.

102:1Of David.
Bless the Lord, my soul,
and all that is within me, His holy name.

102:2Bless the Lord, my soul,
and do not forget all His repayments:

102:3who is gracious toward all your lawless deeds,
who heals all your diseases;

102:4who redeems your life from corruption,
who crowns you with mercy and compassions;

102:5who fills your desire with good things;
your youth will be renewed like an eagle’s.

102:6The Lord does deeds of mercy
and judgment for all who are wronged.

102:7He made His ways known to Moses,
His wishes to the sons of Israel.

102:8The Lord is compassionate and merciful,
patient and abundant in mercy.

102:9He will not be angry to the end,
nor maintain wrath for ever.

102:10He has not dealt with us according to our sins,
nor repaid us according to our lawless deeds,

102:11for according to heaven’s height above the earth,
the Lord strengthened His mercy toward those who fear Him.

102:12As far as the east is distant from the west,
He removed our lawless deeds from us.

102:13As a father has compassion on children,
the Lord had compassion on those who fear Him,

102:14for He knew our formation.
Remember that we are dust.

102:15A man—his days are like grass;
like a flower of the field, so he will flower,

102:16for a wind passed through him, and he will not exist,
and he will no longer recognize his place.

102:17But the Lord’s mercy is from eternity to eternity toward those who fear Him,
and His righteousness toward children’s children,

102:18to those who keep His covenant
and remember His commandments to do them.

102:19The Lord prepared His throne in heaven,
and His kingdom has dominion over all.

102:20Bless the Lord, all His angels,
mighty in strength, doing His word,
so as to hear the voice of His words.

102:21Bless the Lord, all His powers,
His ministers who do His will.

102:22Bless the Lord, all His works,
in every place of His dominion.
Bless the Lord, my soul.

103:1Of David.
Bless the Lord, my soul.
Lord my God, Thou hast become very great;
Thou hast clothed Thyself in praise and dignity,

103:2wrapping Thyself in light like a garment,
stretching out heaven like a hide curtain;

103:3He roofs His upper chambers in waters,
makes clouds His means of ascent,
and walks on the wings of winds.

103:4He makes His angels winds,
and His ministers a burning fire.

103:5He founded the earth on its stability;
it will not be tilted for an age of ages.

103:6The deep is His covering like a garment;
waters will stand upon the mountains.

103:7At Thy rebuke they will flee;
at the voice of Thy thunder they will become afraid.

103:8Mountains rise and plains descend
to the place Thou didst found for them.

103:9Thou didst set a boundary they will not pass,
nor will they return to cover the earth.

103:10He sends springs into the ravines;
waters will pass between the mountains.

103:11They give drink to all the beasts of the field;
wild donkeys will receive it for their thirst.

103:12Upon them the birds of heaven will nest;
from among the rocks they will give voice.

103:13He waters mountains from His upper chambers;
the earth will be filled with the fruit of Thy works.

103:15and wine gladdens the human heart,
to brighten the face with oil,
and bread makes the human heart firm.

103:16The trees of the plain will be filled,
the cedars of Lebanon that He planted;

103:17there sparrows will nest;
the heron’s house leads them.

103:18The high mountains are for deer;
a rock is a refuge for rock rabbits.

103:19He made the moon for seasons;
the sun knew its setting.

103:20Thou didst set darkness, and night came to be;
in it all the beasts of the forest will pass,

103:21young lions roaring to seize prey
and to seek food for themselves from God.

103:22The sun rose, and they gathered,
and they will lie down in their enclosures.

103:23A man will go out to his work
and to his labor until evening.

103:26There ships pass,
and this dragon, which Thou didst form to play with it.

103:27All wait for Thee
to give them food at the right time.

103:28When Thou givest to them, they will gather;
when Thou openest Thy hand, all things will be filled with goodness.

103:29When Thou turnest Thy face away, they will be troubled.
Thou wilt take back their breath, and they will fail
and return to their dust.

103:30Thou wilt send Thy Spirit, and they will be created,
and Thou wilt renew the face of the earth.

103:31Let the Lord’s glory be for ever;
the Lord will rejoice in His works.

103:32He looks upon the earth and makes it tremble;
He touches the mountains, and they smoke.

103:33I will sing to the Lord in my life;
I will make music to my God as long as I exist.

103:34May my meditation be sweet to Him;
as for me, I will rejoice in the Lord.

103:35May sinners vanish from the earth,
and lawless people, so that they no longer exist.
Bless the Lord, my soul.

104:2Sing to Him and make music to Him;
recount all His wonders.

104:3Be praised in His holy name;
let the heart of those seeking the Lord rejoice.

104:4Seek the Lord and be strengthened;
seek His face continually.

104:5Remember His wonders that He did,
His portents and the judgments of His mouth,

104:6offspring of Abraham, His servants,
sons of Jacob, His chosen ones.

104:7He is the Lord our God;
His judgments are in all the earth.

104:8He remembered His covenant for ever,
the word He commanded for a thousand generations,

104:9which He covenanted with Abraham,
and His oath to Isaac;

104:10He established it for Jacob as an ordinance
and for Israel as an everlasting covenant,

104:11saying, To you I will give the land of Canaan,
the measured portion of your inheritance,

104:12when they were small in number,
very few, and sojourners in it,

104:13and passed from nation to nation,
from a kingdom to another people.

104:14He allowed no person to wrong them
and rebuked kings on their behalf:

104:15Do not touch My anointed ones,
and do not act wickedly against My prophets.

104:16He called a famine upon the land;
He shattered every support of bread.

104:17He sent a man ahead of them;
Joseph was sold as a slave.

104:18They humbled his feet in fetters;
his soul passed through iron,

104:19until his word came;
the Lord’s oracle put him through fire.

104:20A king sent and released him;
a ruler of peoples let him go.

104:21He appointed him lord of his house
and ruler of all his possession,

104:22to instruct his rulers as himself
and make his elders wise.

104:23Israel entered Egypt,
and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.

104:24He greatly increased His people
and made them stronger than their enemies.

104:25He turned their heart to hate His people,
to deal deceitfully with His servants.

104:26He sent out Moses His servant,
Aaron whom He chose.

104:27He set among them the words of His signs
and portents in the land of Ham.

104:28He sent out darkness and made it dark,
and they provoked His words.

104:29He turned their waters into blood
and killed their fish.

104:30Their land teemed with frogs
in the chambers of their kings.

104:31He spoke, and dog-flies came,
and gnats throughout all their borders.

104:32He made their rains hail,
consuming fire in their land,

104:33and struck their vines and fig trees
and shattered every tree of their border.

104:34He spoke, and locusts came,
and locust larvae without number,

104:35and devoured all the grass in their land
and devoured the fruit of their land.

104:36He struck every firstborn in their land,
the firstfruits of all their toil,

104:37and brought them out with silver and gold,
and none among their tribes was weak.

104:38Egypt rejoiced at their departure,
for fear of them had fallen upon them.

104:39He spread a cloud as a shelter for them
and fire to light the night for them.

104:40They asked, and quail came,
and He filled them with bread from heaven.

104:41He split a rock, and waters flowed;
rivers traveled through waterless places.

104:42For He remembered His holy word
to Abraham His servant,

104:43and brought His people out in exultation
and His chosen ones in gladness.

104:44He gave them countries of nations,
and they inherited the toils of peoples,

104:45so that they might keep His ordinances
and diligently seek His law.

105:2Who will speak the Lord’s mighty deeds,
make all His praises heard?

105:3Blessed are those who keep judgment
and do righteousness at every time.

105:4Remember us, Lord, with the favor of Thy people;
visit us with Thy salvation,

105:5that we may see the goodness of Thy chosen ones,
rejoice in the gladness of Thy nation,
and be praised with Thine inheritance.

105:6We sinned with our fathers;
we acted lawlessly and unjustly.

105:8He saved them for His name’s sake,
to make His might known.

105:9He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up;
He guided them in the deep as in a wilderness.

105:10He saved them from the hand of those hating them
and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.

105:11Water covered those afflicting them;
not one of them was left.

105:12They believed His words
and sang His praise.

105:13They hurried and forgot His works;
they did not wait for His counsel.

105:14They desired a desire in the wilderness
and tested God in a waterless place.

105:15He gave them their request
and sent fullness into their souls.

105:16They angered Moses in the camp,
and Aaron, the Lord’s holy one.

105:17The earth was opened and swallowed Dathan
and covered Abiram’s assembly.

105:18Fire was kindled in their assembly;
a flame burned up sinners.

105:19They made a calf at Horeb
and bowed down to a carved image.

105:20They exchanged their glory
for the likeness of a calf that eats grass.

105:21They forgot the God who saved them,
who did great things in Egypt,

105:22wonders in the land of Ham,
fearful things at the Red Sea.

105:23He said He would destroy them,
had not Moses His chosen one stood in the breach before Him,
to turn His anger away so He would not destroy.

105:24They treated the desirable land as nothing;
they did not believe His word.

105:25They grumbled in their dwellings;
they did not hear the Lord’s voice.

105:26He lifted His hand to them,
to cast them down in the wilderness,

105:27and to cast their offspring down among the nations,
and scatter them in the countries.

105:28They were initiated to Baal-peor
and ate sacrifices of the dead.

105:29They provoked Him with their practices,
and the falling multiplied among them.

105:30Phinehas stood and made atonement,
and the breaking ceased.

105:31It was reckoned to him as righteousness,
from generation to generation for ever.

105:32They angered Him at the water of contradiction,
and Moses suffered harm because of them,

105:33for they embittered his spirit,
and he issued a command with his lips.

105:34They did not destroy the nations
of which the Lord had spoken to them,

105:35and mixed with the nations
and learned their works.

105:36They served their carved images,
and it became a stumbling block to them.

105:37They sacrificed their sons
and their daughters to demons,

105:39and was defiled by their works,
and they prostituted themselves through their practices.

105:40The Lord was wrathfully angry against His people
and abhorred His inheritance.

105:41He handed them over into nations’ hands,
and those hating them became their masters.

105:42Their enemies afflicted them,
and they were humbled beneath their hands.

105:43Many times He rescued them,
but they provoked Him in their counsel
and were humbled in their lawless deeds.

105:44He saw when they were afflicted,
when He heard their petition.

105:45He remembered His covenant
and changed His purpose according to His abundant mercy,

105:46and granted them compassions
before all who had taken them captive.

105:47Save us, Lord our God,
and gather us together from the nations,
to give thanks to Thy holy name
and boast in Thy praise.

105:48Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from eternity to eternity.
All the people will say, May it be, may it be.

106:2Let those redeemed by the Lord say so,
those He redeemed from the enemy’s hand.

106:3He gathered them from the countries,
from east and west and north and the sea.

106:4They wandered in the wilderness, in a waterless place;
they did not find a road to a city of habitation,

106:5hungry and thirsty;
their soul failed within them.

106:6They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted,
and He rescued them from their distresses,

106:7and guided them into a straight way
to travel to a city of habitation.

106:8Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies
and His wonders to the sons of men,

106:9for He filled an empty soul
and filled a hungry soul with good things.

106:10Those sitting in darkness and death’s shadow,
fettered in poverty and iron,

106:11because they provoked God’s oracles
and spurned the Most High’s counsel,

106:12their heart was humbled in toils;
they grew weak, and there was no helper.

106:13They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted,
and He saved them from their distresses,

106:14and brought them out of darkness and death’s shadow
and broke their bonds apart.

106:15Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies
and His wonders to the sons of men,

106:16for He shattered bronze gates
and broke iron bars.

106:17He helped them out of their lawless way,
for because of their lawless deeds they were humbled.

106:18Their soul abhorred every food,
and they drew near the gates of death.

106:19They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted,
and He saved them from their distresses.

106:20He sent His word and healed them
and rescued them from their destructions.

106:21Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies
and His wonders to the sons of men,

106:22and let them sacrifice a sacrifice of praise
and proclaim His works in exultation.

106:23Those going down into the sea in ships,
doing work on many waters,

106:24they saw the Lord’s works
and His wonders in the depth.

106:25He spoke, and a storm wind stood,
and its waves were raised.

106:27They were troubled and shaken like a drunken man,
and all their wisdom was swallowed up.

106:28They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted,
and He brought them out of their distresses,

106:29and commanded the storm, and it settled into a breeze,
and its waves fell silent.

106:30They rejoiced because they became quiet,
and He guided them to the harbor of their desire.

106:31Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies
and His wonders to the sons of men,

106:32let them exalt Him in an assembly of the people
and praise Him where the elders sit.

106:33He made rivers a wilderness
and outlets of waters thirst,

106:34a fruitful land brine,
because of the wickedness of those inhabiting it.

106:35He made a wilderness lakes of waters
and waterless land outlets of waters,

106:36and settled hungry people there,
and they established a city of habitation,

106:37and sowed fields and planted vineyards
and produced a fruitful crop.

106:38He blessed them, and they multiplied greatly,
and He did not diminish their livestock.

106:39They became few and suffered harm
from the affliction of evils and pain.

106:40Contempt was poured out upon rulers,
and He made them wander in an impassable place, not a road.

106:41He helped the poor out of poverty
and made families like sheep.

106:42The upright will see and rejoice,
and all lawlessness will stop its mouth.

106:43Who is wise and will keep these things,
and will they understand the Lord’s mercies?
107:1A song of a psalm of David.

107:2My heart is ready, God; my heart is ready.
I will sing and make music in my glory.

107:3Awake, psaltery and lyre!
I will awake at dawn.

107:4I will thank Thee among peoples, Lord,
and make music unto Thee among nations,

107:5for Thy mercy is great above the heavens,
and Thy truth reaches the clouds.

107:6Be exalted above the heavens, God,
and Thy glory over all the earth.

107:7So that Thy beloved ones may be rescued,
save with Thy right hand and hear me.

107:8God spoke in His holy place:
I will be exalted and divide Shechem
and measure out the valley of tents.

107:11Who will lead me to a city of enclosure?
Who will guide me as far as Idumea?

107:12Is it not Thou, God, who didst reject us?
Thou wilt not go out, God, with our forces.

107:13Give us help from affliction,
for human salvation is futile.

107:14In God we will act with power,
and He will bring our enemies to nothing.

108:1For the end. Of David. A psalm.
God, do not pass over my praise in silence,

108:2for a sinner’s mouth and a deceitful person’s mouth were opened against me;
they spoke against me with a deceitful tongue,

108:3and surrounded me with words of hatred
and fought me without cause.

108:4Instead of loving me, they were slandering me,
but I was praying.

108:5They set evils against me in exchange for good things
and hatred in exchange for my love.

108:6Appoint a sinner over him,
and let a slanderer stand at his right hand.

108:7When he is judged, may he come out condemned,
and let his prayer become sin.

108:8Let his days become few,
and may another take his oversight.

108:9Let his sons become orphans
and his wife a widow.

108:10Let his sons be shaken and migrate, and let them beg;
let them be cast out from their house sites.

108:11Let a lender search out everything he possesses;
let strangers plunder his toils.

108:12Let no helper exist for him,
nor anyone compassionate toward his orphans.

108:13Let his children be destroyed;
in one generation let his name be erased.

108:14May his fathers’ lawlessness be remembered before the Lord,
and may his mother’s sin not be erased.

108:15Let them be before the Lord continually,
and may their memorial be destroyed from the earth,

108:16because he did not remember to show mercy
and pursued a poor and needy person
and one pierced in heart, to put him to death.

108:17He loved a curse, and it will come to him;
he did not desire blessing, and it will be far from him.

108:19Let it become for him like a garment he puts around himself
and like a belt he continually fastens.

108:20This is the work of those slandering me, from the Lord,
and of those speaking evil against my soul.

108:21But Thou, Lord, Lord, show mercy with me for Thy name’s sake,
for Thy mercy is good.

108:22Rescue me, for I am poor and needy,
and my heart is troubled within me.

108:23Like a shadow as it declines, I was taken away;
I was shaken off like locusts.

108:24My knees grew weak from fasting,
and my flesh was altered because of oil.

108:25I became a reproach to them;
they saw me and shook their heads.

108:26Help me, Lord my God;
save me according to Thy mercy,

108:27and let them know that this is Thy hand
and that Thou, Lord, hast done it.

108:29Let those slandering me wear humiliation
and wrap themselves in their shame like a double cloak.

108:30I will greatly thank the Lord with my mouth
and praise Him among many,

108:31for He stood at a poor person’s right hand,
to save from those pursuing my soul.

109:1Of David. A psalm.
The Lord said to my lord:
Sit at My right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.

109:2The Lord will send out the rod of your power from Zion.
Exercise dominion in the midst of your enemies.

109:4The Lord swore and will not change His purpose:
You are a priest for ever
according to the order of Melchizedek.

109:5The Lord at your right hand
crushed kings on the day of His anger.

109:6He will judge among the nations; He will fill the field with corpses;
He will crush heads over the land of many.

109:7He will drink from a torrent on the way;
therefore he will lift his head.

110:1Hallelujah!
I will give Thee thanks, Lord, with my whole heart,
in the council of the upright and the congregation.

110:2Great are the works of the Lord,
searched out for all His purposes.

110:3Thanksgiving and magnificence are His work,
and His righteousness remains for an age of an age.

110:4He made remembrance of His wonders;
the Lord is merciful and compassionate.

110:5He gave food to those who fear Him;
He will remember His covenant for ever.

110:6He announced the strength of His works to His people,
to give them an inheritance of nations.

110:7The works of His hands are truth and judgment;
all His commandments are faithful,

110:8established for an age of an age,
made in truth and uprightness.

111:2His seed will be powerful in the land;
a generation of the upright will be blessed.

111:3Glory and riches are in his house,
and his righteousness remains for an age of an age.

111:4Light sprang up in darkness for the upright—
merciful, compassionate and righteous.

111:5Kind is the man who has compassion and lends;
he will manage his words with judgment.

111:6For he will never be shaken;
the righteous person will be an everlasting memorial.

111:7He will not fear an evil report;
his heart is ready to hope in the Lord.

111:8His heart is established; he shall certainly not fear,
until he looks upon his enemies.

112:2May the name of the Lord be blessed
from now and for ever.

112:3From the sun’s risings to its settings,
praise the name of the Lord.

112:4The Lord is high above all nations;
His glory is above the heavens.

112:5Who is like the Lord our God,
who dwells in high places,

112:6and looks upon lowly things
in heaven and on earth?

112:7He raises the poor from the ground
and lifts the needy from the dung heap,

112:8to seat him with rulers,
with the rulers of His people.

112:9He settles a barren woman in a house
as a mother of children rejoicing.

113:1Hallelujah.
At Israel’s departure from Egypt,
the house of Jacob from a foreign-speaking people,

113:2Judea became His sanctuary,
Israel His authority.

113:3The sea saw and fled;
the Jordan turned backward.

113:4The mountains skipped like rams,
and the hills like lambs of sheep.

113:5What is it with you, sea, that you fled,
and with you, Jordan, that you withdrew backward?

113:6Mountains, that you skipped like rams,
and hills, like lambs of sheep?

113:7Before the Lord the earth was shaken,
before the God of Jacob,

113:8who turned the rock into pools of water
and the sheer rock into springs of water.

113:9Not to us, Lord, not to us,
but only to Thy name give glory,
because of Thy mercy and Thy truth,

113:10lest the nations say,
“Where is their God?”

113:12The idols of the nations are silver and gold,
works of human hands.

113:13They have a mouth and will not speak;
they have eyes and will not see.

113:14They have ears and will not hear;
they have noses and will not smell.

113:16May those who make them become like them,
and all who have put their trust in them.

113:17The house of Israel hoped in the Lord;
He is their helper and their defender.

113:18The house of Aaron hoped in the Lord;
He is their helper and their defender.

113:19Those who fear the Lord hoped in the Lord;
He is their helper and their defender.

113:21He blessed those who fear the Lord,
the small together with the great.

113:22May the Lord add to you,
to you and to your sons.

113:23You are blessed by the Lord,
who made heaven and earth.

113:24The heaven of heaven belongs to the Lord,
but the earth He gave to the sons of men.

113:25The dead will not praise Thee, Lord,
nor any who descend into Hades,

113:26but we, the living, will bless the Lord

134:8He struck Egypt’s firstborn,
from man to beast.

134:9He sent out signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt,
upon Pharaoh and all his slaves.

134:10He struck many nations
and killed powerful kings,

134:11Sihon king of the Amorites,
Og king of Bashan,
and all Canaan’s kingdoms.

134:12He gave their land as an inheritance,
an inheritance to Israel His people.

134:13Lord, Thy name is for ever;
Lord, Thy memorial is from generation to generation.

134:14For the Lord will judge His people
and be comforted concerning His slaves.

134:15The nations’ idols are silver and gold,
works of human hands.

134:16They have a mouth but will not speak;
they have eyes but will not see.

134:18May those who make them become like them,
and all who trust in them.

134:19House of Israel, bless the Lord;
house of Aaron, bless the Lord.

134:20House of Levi, bless the Lord;
you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord.

134:21Blessed be the Lord from Zion,
He who dwells in Jerusalem.

135:2Give thanks to the God of gods;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:3Give thanks to the Lord of lords;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:4To Him who alone does great wonders;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:5To Him who made the heavens with understanding;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:6To Him who made the earth firm upon the waters;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:7To Him who alone made great lights;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:8the sun for authority over the day;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:9the moon and stars for authority over the night;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:10To Him who struck Egypt with their firstborn;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:11And to Him who brought Israel out from their midst;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:12with a mighty hand and a raised arm;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:13To Him who divided the Red Sea into divisions;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:14And to Him who led Israel through its midst;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:15And to Him who shook Pharaoh and his force into the Red Sea;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:17To Him who struck great kings;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:18And to Him who killed mighty kings;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:19Sihon king of the Amorites;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:20and Og king of Bashan;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:21And to Him who gave their land as an inheritance;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:22an inheritance to Israel His slave;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:23For in our humiliation the Lord remembered us;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:24And He redeemed us from our enemies;
for His mercy is for ever.

135:25He gives food to all flesh;
for His mercy is for ever.

136:1For David.
By Babylon’s rivers, there we sat and wept
when we remembered Zion.

136:2Upon the willows in her midst
we hung our instruments.

136:3For there those who took us captive asked us for words of songs,
and those who led us away for a hymn:
“Sing us some of Zion’s songs.”

136:4How can we sing the Lord’s song
on foreign land?

136:5If I forget you, Jerusalem,
may my right hand be forgotten.

136:7Remember, Lord, Edom’s sons on Jerusalem’s day,
those saying, “Empty her, empty her,
down to the foundation within her!”

136:8Daughter Babylon, miserable one,
happy is the one who will repay you
the repayment you gave us.

136:9Happy is the one who will seize your infants
and dash them against the rock.

137:1For David.
I will thank Thee, Lord, with all my heart,
for Thou heardest the words of my mouth,
and before angels I will make music unto Thee.

137:2I will bow toward Thy holy temple
and thank Thy name for Thy mercy and Thy truth,
for Thou hast magnified Thine utterance above every name.

137:3On whatever day I call Thee, hear me quickly;
Thou wilt greatly attend to me with strength in my soul.

137:4Let all earth’s kings thank Thee, Lord,
for they heard all the words of Thy mouth.

137:5And let them sing in the Lord’s ways,
for great is the Lord’s glory.

137:6For the Lord is high and watches the lowly,
and the lofty He knows from afar.

138:1For the end. A psalm for David.
Lord, Thou didst test me and know me.

138:2Thou knewest my sitting and my rising;
Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.

138:3Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord,
and Thou didst foresee all my ways.
138:4For there is no word on my tongue,

138:5behold, Lord, Thou knewest all things, the last and the first;
Thou didst form me and place Thy hand upon me.

138:6Thy knowledge was made wondrous beyond me;
it grew strong—I cannot reach it.

138:7Where can I go from Thy Spirit,
and where can I flee from Thy face?

138:8If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there;
if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.

138:9if I take up my wings at dawn
and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,

138:10indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me,
and Thy right hand will hold me fast.

138:11And I said, “Then darkness will trample me,
and night is light in my delight.”

138:13For Thou didst acquire my kidneys, Lord;
Thou didst support me from my mother’s womb.

138:15My bone was not hidden from Thee, which Thou madest in secret,
and my substance in earth’s lowest places.

138:17Thy friends were greatly honored by me, God;
their beginnings grew very strong.

138:18I will count them, and they will multiply beyond the sand;
I awoke, and I am still with Thee.

138:19If Thou dost kill sinners, God—
men of blood, turn away from me,

138:20for Thou wilt speak into deliberation;
they will take Thy cities into vanity.

138:21Did I not hate those who hate Thee, Lord,
and melt away over Thine enemies?

138:22I hated them with complete hatred;
they became enemies to me.

138:23Test me, God, and know my heart;
examine me and know my paths,

138:24and see whether a way of lawlessness is in me,
and guide me in an eternal way.
139:1For the end. A psalm for David.

139:2Rescue me, Lord, from an evil person;
deliver me from an unjust man,

139:3those who devised injustices in their heart
and were arraying wars all day.

139:4They sharpened their tongue like a serpent’s;
asp venom is beneath their lips. Diapsalma.

139:7I said to the Lord, “Thou art my God.”
Listen, Lord, to the voice of my petition.

139:8Lord, Lord, power of my salvation,
Thou didst overshadow my head on the day of war.

139:9Do not hand me over to a sinner, Lord, through my desire;
they schemed against me; do not abandon me, lest they rise high. Diapsalma.

139:10The head of their encirclement—
the trouble of their lips will cover them.

139:12A talkative man will not be set straight on the earth;
evils will hunt an unjust man to destruction.

139:13I knew that the Lord will act for the poor person’s judgment
and the needy people’s cause.

139:14Indeed, the righteous will thank Thy name,
and the upright will dwell with Thy presence.

140:1A psalm for David.
Lord, I have cried unto Thee; hear me.
Attend to the voice of my petition when I cry unto Thee.

140:2Let my prayer be directed as incense before Thee,
the lifting of my hands as an evening sacrifice.

140:3Set a guard, Lord, for my mouth
and a restraining door around my lips.

140:4Do not turn my heart toward words of wickedness,
to offer excuses for sins with people who practice lawlessness,
and I will certainly not join with their chosen ones.

140:5A righteous man will discipline me in mercy and correct me,
but let a sinner’s oil not enrich my head,
for still my prayer is amid their good pleasures.

140:6Their judges were swallowed up beside a rock;
they will hear my words, for they became sweet.

140:7Like a clod of earth broken upon the earth,
our bones were scattered beside Hades.

140:8For my eyes are toward Thee, Lord, Lord;
in Thee I hoped—do not take away my soul.

140:9Guard me from the trap they assembled for me
and from the stumbling blocks of those practicing lawlessness.

140:10Sinners will fall into his casting net;
I am alone until I pass by.
141:1Of understanding, of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.

141:2With my voice I cried to the Lord;
with my voice I pleaded with the Lord.

141:3I will pour out my plea before Him;
I will declare my affliction before Him.

141:4When my spirit was failing within me,
Thou knewest my paths.
On this way where I was walking, they hid a trap for me.

141:5I looked to the right and observed, for there was no one recognizing me.
Escape perished from me,
and there is no one seeking my soul.

141:7Attend to my plea, for I was brought very low.
Rescue me from those pursuing me,
for they grew stronger than I.

141:8Bring my soul out of prison, that I may thank Thy name, Lord.
The righteous will wait for me
until Thou repayest me.

142:1A psalm of David, when his son pursues him.
Lord, hear my prayer; give ear to my plea in Thy truth.
Answer me in Thy righteousness.

142:2Do not enter into judgment with Thy servant,
for no one living will be justified before Thee.

142:3For the enemy pursued my soul,
brought my life low to the ground,
made me sit in dark places like those long dead.

142:4My spirit grew despondent within me;
within me my heart was troubled.

142:6I spread out my hands unto Thee;
my soul is like a waterless land for Thee. Diapsalma.

142:7Quickly hear me, Lord; my spirit is spent.
Do not turn Thy face away from me,
or I shall become like those descending to the pit.

142:8Make Thy mercy heard by me in the morning, for I hoped in Thee.
Make known to me, Lord, the way I shall walk,
for unto Thee I lifted my soul.

142:9Take me out from my enemies, Lord,
for I fled unto Thee for refuge.

142:10Teach me to do Thy will, for Thou art my God.
Thy good Spirit will lead me on level ground.

142:11For Thy name’s sake, Lord, Thou wilt give me life;
in Thy righteousness Thou wilt bring my soul out of distress.

142:12In Thy mercy Thou wilt utterly destroy my enemies
and destroy all who distress my soul,
for I am Thy servant.

143:1Of David, concerning Goliath.
Blessed is the Lord, my God,
who trains my hands for battle array, my fingers for war.

143:2My mercy and my refuge, my Helper and my Rescuer,
my Defender, in whom I hoped,
who subjects my people beneath me.

143:3Lord, what is man, that Thou becamest known to him,
or a son of man, that Thou takest account of him?

143:4A man was likened to futility;
his days pass like a shadow.

143:5Lord, bend Thy heavens and descend;
touch the mountains, and they will smoke.

143:6Flash lightning, and Thou wilt scatter them;
send out Thine arrows, and Thou wilt throw them into confusion.

143:8Whose mouth spoke futility,
and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice.

143:9God, I will sing a new song unto Thee;
on a ten-stringed psaltery I will make music unto Thee.

143:10To Him who gives salvation to kings,
who redeems David His servant from an evil sword.

143:11Rescue me and take me out from the hand of foreigners,
whose mouth spoke futility
and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice.

143:12Whose sons are like young plants established in their youth,
their daughters beautified,
adorned all around like the likeness of a sanctuary.

143:15They called happy the people who have these things;
happy the people whose God is the Lord.

144:1A praise of David.
I will exalt Thee, my God, my King,
and bless Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.

144:2Every day I will bless Thee
and praise Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.

144:3Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised;
His greatness has no limit.

144:4Generation after generation will praise Thy works,
and they will declare Thy power.

144:5They will speak of the magnificence of the glory of Thy holiness,
and they will recount Thy wonders.

144:6They will speak of the power of Thy fearsome acts,
and they will recount Thy greatness.

144:7They will pour forth remembrance of the abundance of Thy kindness
and rejoice in Thy righteousness.

144:8Compassionate and merciful is the Lord,
patient and abundant in mercy.

144:9The Lord is kind to all,
and His compassions are over all His works.

144:10Let all Thy works give thanks unto Thee, Lord,
and let Thy holy ones bless Thee.

144:11They will speak of the glory of Thy kingdom
and tell of Thy might,

144:12to make known to the sons of men Thy might
and the glory of the magnificence of Thy kingdom.

144:13Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages,
and Thy lordship endures through every generation.

144:13aFaithful is the Lord in His words,
and holy in all His works.

144:14The Lord supports all who are falling
and raises up all who have been broken down.

144:15The eyes of all hope in Thee,
and Thou givest their food at the right time.

144:16Thou openest Thy hand
and fillest every living creature with good pleasure.

144:17The Lord is righteous in all His ways
and holy in all His works.

144:18The Lord is near to all who call on Him,
to all who call on Him in truth.

144:19He will fulfill the will of those who fear Him;
He will hear their plea and save them.

144:20The Lord guards all who love Him,
and all sinners He will utterly destroy.

144:21My mouth will speak the Lord’s praise,
and let all flesh bless His holy name
for the age and for the age of the age.

145:1Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah.
Praise the Lord, my soul.

145:2I will praise the Lord throughout my life;
I will make music to my God as long as I exist.

145:3Do not trust in rulers
and in sons of men who have no salvation.

145:4His spirit will go out, and he will return to his earth;
on that day all their reasonings will perish.

145:5Happy the one whose Helper is the God of Jacob,
whose hope is in the Lord his God,

145:6who made heaven and earth,
the sea and all that is in them,
who keeps truth for ever,

145:7who does justice for those wronged,
who gives food to the hungry.
The Lord releases those in fetters.

145:10The Lord will reign for ever,
your God, Zion, through every generation.

146:2The Lord builds Jerusalem,
and He will gather the dispersed of Israel.

146:3He heals the brokenhearted
and binds up their fractures.

146:4He numbers multitudes of stars
and calls them all by names.

146:5Great is our Lord, and great is His strength;
His understanding is beyond number.

146:6The Lord takes up the meek,
but brings sinners low to the ground.

146:7Begin singing to the Lord with thanksgiving;
make music to our God with a lyre,

146:8who clothes heaven with clouds,
who prepares rain for the earth,
who makes grass sprout on the mountains
and green growth for the service of humans,

146:9who gives the cattle their food
and to the young ravens who call upon Him.

146:10He will not delight in the horse’s might,
nor does He take pleasure in a man’s shins.

146:11The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear Him
and in those who hope in His mercy.

147:2For He strengthened the bars of your gates;
He blessed your children within you.

147:3He makes your borders peaceful
and fills you with the finest wheat.

147:4He sends His oracle to the earth;
His word will run swiftly,

147:5of Him who gives snow like wool,
who sprinkles mist like ashes,

147:6who casts His ice like morsels;
who will withstand His cold?

147:7He will send His word and melt them;
He will blow His wind, and waters will flow.

147:8He declares His word to Jacob,
His ordinances and judgments to Israel.

147:9He did not do so for any nation,
and He did not disclose His judgments to them.

148:2Praise Him, all His angels;
praise Him, all His powers.

148:3Praise Him, sun and moon;
praise Him, all the stars and the light.

148:4Praise Him, heavens of heavens,
and the water above the heavens.

148:6He established them for the age and for the age of the age;
He set a command, and it will not pass away.

148:7Praise the Lord from the earth,
dragons and all deeps,

148:8fire, hail, snow, ice,
storm wind—all fulfilling His word,

148:9mountains and all hills,
fruit-bearing trees and all cedars,

148:10wild animals and all cattle,
creeping things and winged birds,

148:11kings of the earth and all peoples,
rulers and all judges of the earth,

148:12young men and young women,
old people with younger people.

148:13Let them praise the Lord’s name, for His name alone was exalted;
His praise is over earth and heaven.

148:14He will raise a horn of His people—
a hymn for all His holy ones,
for the children of Israel, a people drawing near to Him.

149:1Hallelujah.
Sing a new song to the Lord,
His praise in the assembly of holy ones.

149:2Let Israel rejoice in the One who made it,
and let Zion’s children exult in their King.

149:3Let them praise His name in a chorus;
with tambourine and psaltery let them make music to Him.

149:4For the Lord takes pleasure in His people,
and He will exalt the meek in salvation.

149:5Holy ones will boast in glory
and rejoice upon their beds.

149:6Exaltations of God in their throat,
and two-edged swords in their hands,

149:7to execute vengeance among the nations,
reproofs among the peoples,

149:8to bind their kings in fetters
and their glorious ones in iron handcuffs,

149:9to execute upon them a written judgment.
This is glory for all His holy ones.

150:2Praise Him for His mighty acts;
praise Him according to the abundance of His greatness.

150:3Praise Him with the sound of a trumpet;
praise Him with psaltery and lyre.

150:4Praise Him with tambourine and chorus;
praise Him with strings and instrument.

150:5Praise Him with well-sounding cymbals;
praise Him with cymbals of a shout.

150:6Let every breath praise the Lord.
Hallelujah.

151:1This psalm is personally written concerning David and is outside the number, when he fought Goliath in single combat.
I was small among my brothers
and younger in my father’s house;
I was shepherding my father’s sheep.

151:2My hands made an instrument;
my fingers fitted a psaltery.

151:3And who shall tell my Lord?
He Himself is Lord; He Himself hears.

151:4He Himself sent out His angel
and took me from my father’s sheep
and anointed me with the oil of His anointing.

151:5My brothers were handsome and tall,
but the Lord took no pleasure in them.

151:6I went out to meet the foreigner,
and he cursed me by his idols.

151:7But I drew the sword he carried,
cut off his head,
and removed reproach from the sons of Israel.
